The core of this algorithm lies in its ability to dynamically adjust the genetic algorithm's parameters based on data feedback and model error. Traditional genetic algorithms often require manual parameter tuning, which can be time-consuming and limit the algorithm's adaptability. This work introduces a mechanism that automatically adjusts parameters during the optimization process, resulting in improved optimization results and enhanced robustness. We explore the design and implementation of this dynamic adaptation, demonstrating its effectiveness through a series of benchmark optimization problems. The focus is on providing a practical and automated solution to the challenges inherent in traditional genetic algorithm optimization.

title: Distributed Differential Privacy with Adaptive Noise Scheduling
abstract: This paper introduces a novel distributed differential privacy (DP) algorithm employing adaptive noise scheduling. Traditional DP approaches frequently rely on fixed noise levels, often resulting in a significant trade-off between privacy and utility. Our method addresses this limitation by dynamically adjusting the noise level based on both local data heterogeneity and global system statistics. This allows for a more nuanced approach, reducing overall noise while preserving strong privacy guarantees. The core claim is that adaptive noise scheduling provides a superior balance between privacy and accuracy in distributed settings. We present a formal framework for this algorithm, incorporating key concepts such as local sensitivity, global sensitivity, and the Laplace mechanism. The proposed scheme is analyzed rigorously, demonstrating its ability to maintain strong DP guarantees under varying system conditions. The design focuses on minimizing the impact of data heterogeneity, a common challenge in distributed DP, and offers a practical solution for improving the efficiency of DP computations in real-world scenarios. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through theoretical analysis and outline its potential for applications in various distributed data processing tasks.

title: A Simulated Annealing-Based Program Proving System
abstract: This paper presents a novel system for program proving leveraging the Simulated Annealing (SA) algorithm. The core claim is that SA can effectively address the search space challenges inherent in program proving, ultimately enhancing both proof efficiency and reliability. The system models program proving as an optimization problem, utilizing SA's ability to explore diverse solution paths through random jumps within the search space. Furthermore, heuristic rules are incorporated to accelerate this exploration. This approach contrasts with traditional program proving methods which often rely on deterministic algorithms and substantial computational resources. We demonstrate the potential of SA to provide a more robust and efficient search strategy, particularly for complex program verification tasks. The system's architecture and underlying principles are detailed, focusing on the algorithmic components and the strategic implementation of SA. The effectiveness of the system is discussed through a conceptual framework, outlining the key elements and anticipated benefits.

title: Autonomy-Driven Evolutionary Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces the Autonomy-Driven Evolutionary Algorithm (ADEA), a novel approach to evolutionary computation designed to address the limitations of traditional evolutionary algorithms in dynamic and unpredictable environments. The core concept of ADEA revolves around embedding an "evolutionary engine" within the algorithm itself, allowing it to autonomously modify its internal structure and parameters based on adaptive fitness evaluations. This mechanism aims to enhance the algorithm's adaptability and robustness by enabling it to continuously refine its own design. The algorithm leverages a population-based search strategy with a key difference: individuals aren't just evaluated for their solutions, but also for the *effectiveness* of their internal design. This leads to a self-optimizing process, where successful designs are replicated and refined, while less effective ones are discarded. This paper details the architecture, key components, and theoretical underpinnings of ADEA, highlighting its potential advantages over conventional evolutionary algorithms. We explore the mathematical framework underpinning the adaptive selection and parameter adjustment processes, demonstrating how ADEA achieves a higher degree of autonomy and efficiency in tackling complex optimization challenges. The effectiveness of ADEA is illustrated through a series of conceptual examples and a discussion of potential applications.

title: Automated Program Code Optimization Based on Genetic Algorithms
abstract: This paper explores the application of genetic algorithms (GAs) to automate the optimization of program code. The core claim is that GAs can effectively enhance program performance and efficiency through iterative refinement of code. The proposed mechanism involves representing program code as a genetic encoding and employing a GA to evolve this encoding. This approach allows for the automatic discovery of optimized code structures. This work details a methodology for implementing this approach, focusing on the theoretical foundations and outlining a potential framework. The paper avoids experimental results, concentrating on the conceptual design and algorithmic principles. The presented framework offers a novel approach to software optimization, potentially leading to significant improvements in various computing domains.

title: ##拓扑信息论的量子纠错码设计
abstract: This paper explores the application of topological information theory to the design of quantum error correction codes. Quantum information transfer is inherently vulnerable to noise and decoherence, necessitating robust error correction techniques. Traditional error correction methods rely on classical algorithms, which often struggle to maintain security against these vulnerabilities. We propose a novel approach based on topological information theory, offering a fundamentally different paradigm for encoding and decoding quantum information. The core mechanism involves constructing quantum codes that leverage the inherent robustness of topological states, enabling significantly enhanced security and improved error correction efficiency. This paper details the design process, mathematical foundations, and preliminary results demonstrating the potential of this approach.

title: Emergent Semantics: A Distributed Computation Model
abstract: This paper proposes a novel semantic model based on distributed computation, inspired by the emergent semantics observed in biological neural networks. The core idea is to simulate the complex dynamics of neural networks through a multi-agent system, where each agent specializes in processing specific semantic information. Through orchestrated collaboration and competition among these agents, we aim to achieve emergent and evolving semantics. Traditional semantic models often struggle with capturing the dynamic nature of meaning and the ability of systems to generate novel concepts. This model offers a fundamentally different approach by leveraging the inherent parallelism and self-organization principles found in biological systems. We define key components of this system, including agent architecture, communication protocols, and mechanisms for promoting both cooperation and competition, ultimately leading to a more robust and adaptable semantic representation. The theoretical framework is presented, along with a discussion of potential applications and future research directions.

title: Topological Quantum State Based Quantum Key Distribution Protocol
abstract: This paper proposes a novel Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) protocol leveraging the inherent properties of topological quantum states. The core claim is to enhance key security and transmission distance by exploiting the robustness offered by topological protection. The protocol utilizes entanglement between topological qubits and employs phase control and measurement to achieve secure key encryption and distribution. The fundamental mechanism relies on the high fidelity of topological quantum states to mitigate eavesdropping attacks. We demonstrate that this approach overcomes the limitations of conventional QKD protocols that are susceptible to environmental noise due to weak qubit interactions. The protocol offers a promising pathway for long-distance QKD, particularly in environments where maintaining the coherence of individual qubits is challenging. The key mathematical elements of the protocol are presented, including the state preparation, entanglement distribution, key sifting, and error correction phases. The theoretical analysis highlights the security advantages derived from the topological protection mechanism.

title: Adaptive Regularized Learning (ARLS)
abstract: This paper introduces Adaptive Regularized Learning (ARLS), a novel approach to neural network training that addresses the limitations of traditional regularization methods. The core claim is that regularization within neural networks can, and should, dynamically adjust based on the underlying data distribution. ARLS achieves this through a mechanism rooted in statistical learning theory, designing an algorithm that adapts the regularization parameter in real-time. The key innovation lies in abandoning the fixed regularization parameters prevalent in conventional methods, allowing for more effective model training and improved generalization performance. This document details the theoretical foundation, the algorithmic design, and the anticipated benefits of ARLS. The primary goal is to demonstrate a method that more closely aligns regularization with the actual complexity of the data, leading to superior model outcomes.

title: Quantum Geometry and Topology: A New Approach to Quantum Computation
abstract: This paper explores the intersection of quantum geometry and topology, investigating its potential to revolutionize quantum computation. We propose a novel framework leveraging quantum geometry to model and manipulate high-dimensional topological structures, thereby offering new tools and algorithms for quantum information processing. The core claim is that this integrated approach, combining quantum geometry with topology information theory, will significantly enhance the capabilities of quantum computers. This research aims to provide a robust and flexible foundation for exploring complex quantum systems and developing advanced quantum algorithms.

title: Adaptive Phase Space Self-Organizing Model
abstract: This paper introduces an Adaptive Phase Space Self-Organizing Model (APSM) designed to facilitate the self-organization and optimization of complex systems, with a particular focus on neural network training. The model leverages adaptive phase transformation techniques to dynamically adjust the phase values of network nodes and connections, enabling a mechanism for self-organization and optimization that surpasses traditional static approaches. The core claim is that the APSM provides a novel approach to address the challenges of complex system dynamics and enables enhanced training performance for neural networks. We present a theoretical framework and preliminary results demonstrating the efficacy of this model in simulating and optimizing network structures.

title: Hardware-Assisted Spatial Memory Safety for Shared GPU Accelerators: A Pointer Tagging Co-Design with Analytical and Synthesis-Level Evaluation
abstract: Graphics processing units (GPUs) underpin high-performance computing, but device partitioning does not ensure that an in-context pointer remains within its allocation. We present a hardware–software co-design whose 16-bit tag uses odd parity and fail-safe class encoding. It combines a variable-precision extent, an aligned CRC checker, and an exact-bounds micro-cache. For 200,000 log-uniform requests from 16 B to 1 TiB, mean Class 4 fragmentation is 1.638%, versus 27.733% for power-of-two encoding. The seven-bit aligned signature has full GF(2) rank and a 1/128 non-adaptive collision rate; its deterministic window is exactly one through three regions and tight at four. Exhaustive testing rejects every one-bit tag corruption, while two-bit analysis demonstrates why parity is not adversarial authentication. A SAT-equivalent endpoint rewrite reduces Class 3 generic depth from 60 to 24 levels. A fail-closed 32-lane Class 4 topology detects nonuniform active-lane tags in hardware; for uniform tags, it reduces generic CMOS cost from 155,200 to 72,872 transistor equivalents (53.05%) and depth from 67 to 61 levels. Official SASS traces provide an analytical exposure bound rather than native simulation; a separate pre-layout 45 nm mapping is reported only as a timing sensitivity experiment.

title: Reconstruction-aware urban crime analytics from incomplete judicial records using heterogeneous graph temporal imputation
abstract: Introduction: Incomplete judicial records constrain reliable crime analytics because missing attributes, heterogeneous case descriptions, mixed variable types, and imbalanced charge distributions reduce their analytical value. This study developed a reconstruction-aware framework for drug-crime charge classification from incomplete judicial records. Methods: Drug-related judicial documents from Chengdu, China, covering 2014-2021 were screened, cleaned, and converted into structured person-level observations. The final dataset comprised 12,620 valid documents and 15,184 observations with 16 structured features. A Heterogeneous Graph Convolution Temporal Autoencoder (HetGConv-TAE) was developed to jointly model heterogeneous case-attribute relations and temporal changes in case composition. Performance was evaluated under 10%, 20%, and 30% controlled missingness, followed by XGBoost charge classification and SHAP interpretation. Results: HetGConv-TAE achieved the best mean reconstruction performance across conventional, static graph, temporal, and relational graph baselines. XGBoost trained on HetGConv-TAE reconstructed data achieved weighted F1 scores close to 80% and ROC-AUC values above 90%. SHAP analysis identified drug weight, place category, and administrative district as the most influential predictors across charge categories. Discussion: Combining label-excluded heterogeneous graph reconstruction, temporal encoding, downstream classification, and interpretable analysis improves the analytical usefulness of incomplete judicial archives. The framework is intended to support data-quality assessment and aggregate public-safety research rather than automated legal decision-making.

title: MpSub: A Momentum $p$-Dimensional Subspace Trust-Region Method for Derivative-Free Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models
abstract: Full-parameter fine-tuning of large language models has substantial memory costs because backpropagation stores activations and gradients. Zeroth-order optimization avoids this by estimating update directions from loss evaluations, but existing methods require tuning a sensitive learning rate for each model and task. We propose the momentum $p$-dimensional subspace trust-region method (MpSub). At each iteration, MpSub searches within a $p$-dimensional subspace: one direction preserves historical momentum from the most recent accepted step, while the remaining directions explore via fresh random sampling. The subspace gradient is estimated by central differences, a trial step is computed from a linear trust-region model, and the trust-region radius adapts according to the agreement between predicted and observed loss reduction, eliminating the learning rate. For LLM fine-tuning, evaluations within an iteration share a minibatch, and directions are regenerated in place from seeds, using forward passes alone. For smooth deterministic objectives under unorthogonalized Gaussian directions, we bound the finite-difference error, quantify gradient energy captured by the subspace, and prove that $\lim_{k\to\infty} \|\nabla f(x_k)\|_2 = 0$ almost surely under a safeguarded radius update. Under a matched budget of 8,400 training-objective forward passes, we fine-tune OPT-125M and OPT-350M on CommitmentBank. With the same preset parameters at both model sizes, MpSub attains mean test accuracies of 0.673 and 0.690 over three seeds, matching tuned MeZO (0.685) without any learning-rate search.

title: Beyond Task Success: Stage-Wise Reliability of World Model Planning under Sensing Degradation
abstract: In world model planning, sensing inputs pass through an encoder and predictor before affecting planner decisions, so final task success alone cannot reveal where sensing disturbances attenuate or persist in the pipeline. We apply 10 visual and temporal sensing degradations to a world model planner and track their effects across representation, future prediction, planner preference, and physical outcome using paired evaluation on the same 50 tasks. The relative impact of degradations was not preserved across stages: large representation shifts could attenuate downstream, while smaller initial shifts could persist to the outcome, and internal-response ordering did not directly match physical-outcome ordering. Temporal degradations also showed distinct patterns: even with similar overall changes in observation history, responses differed substantially with the location of corrupted information and the planner's actual exposure. This non-uniform stage-wise response was also observed in secondary evaluations with another manipulation task and a different world model. Stage-wise diagnosis can therefore identify where sensing disturbances attenuate or persist and help prioritize subsequent model verification and sensing mitigation.

title: Term extraction for user profiling: Evaluation by the user
abstract: We compared three term scoring methods in their ability to extract descriptive terms from a knowledge worker's document collection. We compared the methods in two different evaluation scenarios, both from the perspective of the user: a perterm evaluation, and a holistic (term cloud) evaluation. We found that users tend to prefer a term scoring method that gives a higher score to multi-word terms than to single-word terms. In addition, users are not always consistent in their judgements of term profiles, if they are presented in different forms (as list or as cloud).

title: Preservation of Judgment Levels in Non-Closed Reasoning: A Time Restoration Theory 4.0 Account of Reasoning in Artificial Intelligence
abstract: 人工智慧推理(reasoning)研究關注模型如何利用前提、中間結果與表示形成後續判定。近年的大型語言模型與長鏈思維(long chain-of-thought)研究顯示,推理長度、反思、推理軌跡選擇與中間步驟忠實性已成為重要問題;然而,推理過程能夠持續生成,並不等同於其中每一項既有判定都可無條件取得新的成立範圍。 本研究以時間還原理論 4.0(TRT 4.0)為直接理論來源,將其必要層級、共同成立、高階總和表示、表示再進入與非封閉等既有關係映射至人工智慧推理問題。本文提出的核心問題是:已成立的不同關係如何共同進入後續推理,而在推理持續生成的過程中保持其原有判定層級,並允許新的判定另行成立,而不使既有判定資格因共同參與或推理延續而無條件跨層轉移? 本文的核心理論結果是:推理可以延續,但既有判定的成立位置不能僅因其被表示、共同承載或重新進入後續生成而自動擴張。TRT 4.0 的 P_{κ_a} ⇏ P_{κ_b}(κ_a ≠ κ_b)在本文中被映射為推理中的判定層級限制;Joint 與 Agg 可描述多項已成立關係的共同參與與共同承載,但不創造新的成立關係;Enter 可描述表示重新進入後續生成,但再進入本身不授予新的判定資格;非封閉則允許後續生成而不保證唯一或必然正確的終點。 本研究進一步提出「判定資格漂移」作為一項候選 reasoning failure 描述:若某一內容只在 κ_a 上成立,卻在缺乏新的成立條件時,因推理延續而被當作已在 κ_b 上成立,則構成本文所關注的跨層判定問題。此概念不是 TRT 4.0 原有謂詞,也不是所有推理錯誤的普遍定義。本文未進行模型訓練、資料集實驗、神經網路內部測量或新的形式邏輯證明,因此不主張 TRT 已解決人工智慧推理問題。

title: Quantum-Enhanced Chaos Modeling
abstract: Quantum-enhanced chaos modeling aims to significantly accelerate the simulation and prediction of chaotic systems by exploiting quantum phenomena such as superposition and entanglement. This paper explores the potential of a novel 'Quantum Resonance Engine' to enhance chaos dynamics through the manipulation of quantum states, offering a potentially transformative approach to computational chaos analysis. We outline the core mechanism, present preliminary theoretical considerations, and discuss the challenges and future research directions for this ambitious endeavor. The goal is to provide a practical framework for accelerating the study of complex, nonlinear dynamical systems.

title: Distributed Consensus Algorithms for Quantum State Preparation
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of achieving robust distributed consensus within quantum systems, focusing on the preparation of quantum states. The core challenge stems from the inherent fragility of quantum states due to decoherence and the limitations imposed by communication channels in distributed environments. We propose a new framework for consensus algorithms specifically designed for quantum state preparation, leveraging entanglement-assisted communication and advanced error correction methods. These algorithms are constructed to mitigate the effects of noise and ensure reliable agreement among distributed quantum nodes. We present a theoretical analysis of the proposed algorithms, outlining their key characteristics, limitations, and potential improvements. The work contributes to the growing field of quantum distributed computing by providing a novel approach to achieving consensus, a critical requirement for building complex and reliable quantum networks. We explore the impact of different parameters on the performance of the algorithms and suggest avenues for future research.

title: Adaptive High-Dimensional Probability Space
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm for adaptive high-dimensional probability space modeling, designed to enhance prediction accuracy through automated parameter and structural adjustment based on learned data. The core of this approach is a dynamically evolving model that adapts to the data distribution, addressing the limitations of static, fixed models. We propose a framework incorporating a learning component that iteratively refines the model's parameters and structure to optimize performance. This framework aims to improve robustness and generalization capabilities compared to traditional methods. The paper details the algorithm's design, the theoretical justification for its effectiveness, and provides a preliminary implementation demonstrating its capabilities on a simplified dataset.

title: Adaptive Bayesian Networks for Causal Discovery with Symbolic Reasoning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to causal discovery utilizing Adaptive Bayesian Networks (ABNs) coupled with symbolic reasoning. Traditional data-driven causal discovery methods often struggle with spurious correlations and lack interpretability. This work addresses these limitations by integrating domain expertise and logical constraints through a symbolic reasoning engine. The Adaptive Bayesian Network algorithm dynamically adjusts its structure based on both statistical evidence and symbolic knowledge, leading to more accurate and interpretable causal models. The core idea is to augment Bayesian network learning with a mechanism capable of identifying causal relationships based on predefined rules and logical constraints. We introduce a framework where the network's structure evolves adaptively, incorporating symbolic reasoning to resolve ambiguities and guide the discovery process. The resulting ABNs offer improved robustness and interpretability compared to purely data-driven approaches, particularly in domains with rich background knowledge. The algorithm is designed to handle uncertainty effectively, leveraging Bayesian inference and continually updating the network structure based on new observations and symbolic constraints. This research contributes to a more reliable and transparent method for uncovering causal relationships from observational data.

title: Quantum Topological Simulation via Entanglement
abstract: Quantum topological simulation offers a novel approach to studying complex topological structures, leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement to achieve precision and efficiency. This paper explores the design and implementation of a quantum entanglement-based framework for topology simulation, focusing on the ability to accurately model topological evolution and utilize topological features for calculations. We present a core mechanism that establishes a quantum entanglement-driven model, employing entanglement for precise simulation and utilizing topological features for deeper understanding. The paper details the significance of this method for tackling challenging topological systems, highlighting its potential for advancing our comprehension of these intricate phenomena.

title: Temporal Graph Embedding with Predictive Relational Context
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to temporal graph embedding that leverages predicted relational context to enhance the representation of dynamic graphs. Traditional temporal graph embedding methods often treat the temporal evolution of a graph as a static problem, overlooking the crucial aspect of how relationships themselves change over time. Our proposed method utilizes a recurrent neural network (RNN) architecture to learn node and edge embeddings while simultaneously predicting future relational connections. A variational autoencoder (VAE) is incorporated to constrain the embedding space and ensure smooth transitions across the temporal dimension. The core idea is that understanding the *prediction* of relationships, alongside the observed relationships, provides a richer and more robust embedding. We demonstrate that this predictive modeling significantly improves the quality of graph embeddings compared to static embedding techniques. The key contributions of this work include a novel RNN architecture specifically designed for temporal graph embedding with relational prediction, and a VAE-based approach for regularizing the embedding space. This framework allows for capturing temporal dependencies and dynamics within graphs, leading to improved performance in downstream graph-based tasks.

title: 基于动态网络的优化算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel optimization algorithm based on dynamic networks. Traditional optimization methods often rely on static parameter adjustments, limiting their effectiveness in dynamic environments. This research introduces a framework that dynamically adjusts optimization parameters based on network topology changes, enabling real-time optimization and superior performance in complex scenarios. The core mechanism leverages the inherent properties of dynamic networks to iteratively refine the optimization process, achieving more efficient global optimization. The proposed algorithm demonstrates significant improvements in various optimization tasks, highlighting its potential for applications across diverse fields.

title: 基于自适应自律的量子态演化算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum state evolution algorithm based on adaptive self-regulation. Traditional quantum state evolution algorithms often struggle with complex systems and require significant manual tuning. This work introduces a framework where the evolution rules are dynamically adjusted based on the system's dynamics, offering a more robust and adaptable approach. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this algorithm in stabilizing quantum states within complex environments. The core mechanism involves employing self-regulating parameters to guide the state evolution, mitigating the inherent challenges of quantum systems. This algorithm promises increased efficiency and control over quantum states, particularly in challenging scenarios.

abstract: This paper introduces an innovative approach to dynamic topology modeling, leveraging the power of adaptive quantum algorithms to simulate complex systems and dynamically adjust model parameters. AQDMM offers a fundamentally new paradigm by employing quantum algorithms to create and refine complex topological structures, enabling more accurate and efficient modeling. This research explores the design and implementation of AQDMM, highlighting its potential for simulating a wide range of systems exhibiting dynamic topology. The paper details the core mechanism, focusing on quantum algorithms for topology representation and adaptive parameter adjustment. The resulting model demonstrates significant improvements in simulation accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods, particularly for systems with intricate topological relationships. The study emphasizes the benefits of this approach in tackling problems requiring real-time adaptation to dynamic systems.

This work proposes a novel approach utilizing neural networks to learn matrix parameters and automatically adjust them based on the input, resulting in more accurate and robust matrix representations. The method leverages the power of neural networks to achieve this dynamic adaptation, offering a significant advancement over static matrix learning techniques.

title: RouteGuard: Cost-Aware Abstention for LLM-Based IT Ticket Classification — Camera-Ready Artifact
abstract: Camera-ready update for ICTAI 2026. This version adds the post-hoc 16-setting cost-parameter sensitivity analysis and its corresponding verification artifacts. Calibration-selected policies beat both trivial policies in 14 of 16 evaluated settings. The primary predeclared result under the illustrative cost setting (0, 1, 5) remains unchanged: the TF-IDF + logistic-regression policy reduces modeled test cost by 38.1%, with a 95% paired-bootstrap confidence interval of 35.7% to 40.4%. Camera-ready artifact for "Cost-Aware Abstention for LLM-Based IT Ticket Classification" (IEEE ICTAI 2026). The archive contains the evaluation framework and the audited numerical evidence behind the paper's tables and figures. It pairs with the source repository at https://github.com/sachinkg12/RouteGuard, pinned at commit 793b337b0f5a4a417a137cf8d89a29d4b6ca8991. CONTENTS - code/ — the evaluation framework, configurations, tests, and analysis scripts, identical to the pinned commit. - code/artifacts/ictai2026/ — the scoped public claim record, the audited claim manifest, its verification receipt, sanitized text-free LLM prediction and confidence vectors, the sanitized Table II common-subset inputs, and the aggregate near-duplicate diagnostic. - code/outputs/ — the frozen run bundles behind the reported results. - paper_artifacts/camera_ready_results/ — aggregate result tables, the claim manifest, and the audit report. - MANIFEST.sha256, ARCHIVE_METADATA.json, ENVIRONMENT.txt, CLAIM_ARTIFACT_LEDGER.md, SUPPLEMENT_README.md. VERIFICATION python3.14 -m venv .venv.venv/bin/python -m pip install -e '.[test]' -c requirements-camera-ready-lock.txt.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q.venv/bin/python scripts/verify_camera_ready_manifest.py --paper-dir ../paper_artifacts.venv/bin/python scripts/verify_public_claims.py --artifact-dir artifacts/ictai2026.venv/bin/python scripts/baselines_on_llm_subsample.py NOT INCLUDED The evaluation dataset is not redistributed. It is the public IT Service Ticket Classification Dataset, version 1 (CC0), available at https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/adisongoh/it-service-ticket-classification-dataset/versions/1 and expected at data/it_service_tickets.csv. No ticket text, raw prompt or response logs, credentials, or the IEEE Version of Record are included. SCOPE Reported cost reductions are specific to this dataset and to an illustrative cost model (c_ok, c_triage, c_wrong) = (0, 1, 5). The work is an evaluation framework, not a new abstention algorithm or a deployment certification. LICENSING Source code is MIT licensed. Result artifacts are available under CC BY 4.0. title: Bio-Inspired Algorithms for Quantum Computing Resource Allocation
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to quantum computing resource allocation by leveraging principles derived from biological neural networks. The core idea centers on mimicking the resource competition and cooperation mechanisms observed in biological systems to optimize the distribution and scheduling of quantum computational resources. We propose a resource management system built upon adaptive competition and cooperation algorithms, modeled using neural networks to dynamically allocate quantum resources. The system's architecture incorporates elements like synaptic plasticity, neuronal firing rates, and signaling pathways to create a robust and efficient allocation strategy. This research demonstrates the potential for bio-inspired algorithms to significantly improve the efficiency and performance of quantum computing, addressing key challenges in scaling quantum systems. The proposed framework offers a promising path towards more intelligent and adaptive resource management in the evolving field of quantum computation.

title: Quantum Information Evolution Theory Adaptive Algorithm Design
abstract: Quantum information evolution theory offers a novel approach to algorithm design, particularly in the context of quantum systems. This paper proposes a robust and adaptable algorithm design method based on quantum state evolution. The core mechanism involves dynamically adjusting quantum state parameters, such as qubit entanglement and interaction strength, to respond to the system's dynamic evolution. This adaptive capability significantly improves algorithm efficiency and stability compared to traditional approaches. This research presents a comprehensive framework for implementing this evolution-aware algorithm design, demonstrating its potential for enhancing quantum computation.

abstract: This paper investigates the potential of utilizing quantum-enhanced geometric transformations to improve the precision of quantum state manipulation. The core claim is to develop a novel method that employs quantum superposition to subtly influence geometric changes within quantum states. We explore the theoretical underpinnings of this approach and outline a potential pathway toward enhanced quantum computation and data representation. This research is driven by the desire to push the boundaries of current quantum technologies by exploring unconventional methods for manipulating the fundamental structure of quantum systems.

title: Jincheng Zhang
abstract: The optimization process is a crucial element in many scientific and engineering disciplines, driving advancements across diverse fields. Traditional optimization algorithms often rely on precise mathematical models, which can struggle to effectively handle dynamic and uncertain environments. This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on probabilistic logic, designed to dynamically adjust parameters based on the probability distribution of the environment, thereby enhancing adaptability. We present a framework where the optimization objective is transformed into a probability distribution, enabling the algorithm to better respond to unpredictable fluctuations. This approach offers a significant departure from conventional methods, capitalizing on the inherent strengths of probabilistic modeling to achieve more robust and efficient solutions. The paper details the core mechanism, explores its implementation, and provides a preliminary evaluation of its performance across a range of scenarios.

title: ローカル LLM を用いた数学学習支援アプリの設計と実装
abstract: 近年,AIを学習の補助に用いる学生が増えている.しかし,無料プランと有料プランでは利用できるモデルや機能に差があり,費用の負担が学習機会の格差につながる可能性がある.そこで私たちは,有料のAIサービスを継続して利用することが難しい生徒にもAIを用いた学習環境を届けるため,数学学習支援アプリを開発した.このアプリは,大規模言語モデル(large language model,LLM)を利用者の端末で実行するローカルLLMを採用している.質問ごとの外部の推論サービスへの利用料を避け,アプリを無料で提供する構成とした.本稿で紹介する「AI先生 高校数学」は,文章または写真による質問を受け付け,教材を参照しながら日本語で解き方を説明する.実装では質問の内容を整理する段階と説明を生成する段階を分け,それぞれに必要な情報をモデルに入力する.開発環境で比較したところ,質問の整理に不要な指示を除くと回答が現れるまでの待ち時間が短縮した.また,iOSへの実装ではモデルの呼び出し方と実行条件を調べ,開発環境との違いに起因する不具合を特定した.本研究では,無料で利用できる数学学習支援を実現するための設計と,開発過程で生じた問題への対処を報告する.

title: Where to Look and What to Use: Retrieve-Localize-Generate for Long-Term Conversational Memory Question Answering
abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) enables large language models (LLMs) to answer questions by accessing external knowledge and has been widely adopted for long-term conversational memory question answering. However, existing methods suffer from two key challenges: (1) fragmented evidence scattered across temporally distant sessions, and (2) noisy content within retrieved sessions that triggers the lost-in-the-middle effect. To address these challenges, we propose MemLoc, a unified Retrieve-Localize-Generate framework for long-term conversational memory QA. For retrieval, MemLoc decomposes each session into multi-granularity memory units and performs query routing via an inner-memory graph with entropy-based granularity selection. It further models cross-session semantic and temporal dependencies through a cross-memory graph, enabling coarse-to-fine retrieval of top-K relevant memory candidates. For localization, we introduce a reasoning-based evidence locator trained with Self-reflective Hint Policy Optimization (SHPO), which performs progressive refinement by extracting query-relevant fragments within memory units to suppress noise and reranking across candidates to remove redundancy, producing a compact evidence set with lightweight location IDs. For generation, these IDs act as precise grounding signals that guide the LLM to the correct memory positions, mitigating the lost-in-the-middle effect while preserving original contextual integrity. Extensive experiments on four benchmarks demonstrate that MemLoc achieves state-of-the-art retrieval accuracy and response quality while maintaining efficiency. Our code is available at: https://github.com/Nikol-coder/MemLoc.

title: Ontology Matching for Big Data Applications in the Smart Dairy Farming Domain.
abstract: This paper addresses the use of ontologies for combining different sensor data sources to enable big data analysis in the dairy farming domain. We have made existing data sources accessible via linked data RDF mechanisms using OWL ontologies on Virtuoso and D2RQ triple stores. In addition, we have created a common ontology for the domain and mapped it to the existing ontologies of the different data sources. Furthermore, we verified this mapping using the ontology matching tools HerTUDA, AML, LogMap and YAM++. Fi-nally, we have enabled the querying of the combined set of data sources using SPARQL on the common ontology.

title: Exact Determination of the Binary Covering-Sequence Length L(12,3)
abstract: Technical report, exhaustive-search software, and source-bound evidence establishing L(12,3) = 36. Independent C++ and Rust traversals exclude all 68,719,476,734 binary sequences of positive lengths 1 through 35 through 506,526,514 rotation-reversal-complement representatives. A public attributed 36-bit witness is independently verified. Project-original material is MIT licensed; the normalized attributed witness remains under Apache-2.0.

title: 基于动态拓扑的机器学习算法的参数调整算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel parameter adjustment algorithm based on dynamic topology, designed to enhance the training of machine learning models by dynamically adapting model parameters to the inherent structure of the input data. Traditional machine learning algorithms often operate in a static manner, limiting their ability to effectively model complex data. The proposed algorithm leverages the concept of dynamic topology to continuously refine the model's parameters, resulting in improved model performance and robustness. We present a theoretical framework and empirical validation demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach. The core mechanism involves mapping the input data to a dynamic topology, enabling the algorithm to iteratively adjust parameters in response to these topological relationships. This adaptive adjustment process significantly improves model generalization and efficiency.

title: Dynamic Topology Transformations via Quantum Computing: A Novel Approach to Topological Simplification
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic topology transformation technique leveraging quantum computing to streamline and optimize topological structures, thereby reducing computational complexity. Traditional topological transformation methods are often limited by the computational demands of classical algorithms. Quantum computing offers unique capabilities, particularly in the manipulation of quantum states and entanglement, that can significantly accelerate these transformations. We propose a new algorithm employing quantum entanglement and superposition to iteratively refine topological structures, effectively simplifying them and minimizing the required computational resources. The core mechanism involves a sequence of quantum operations designed to induce specific topological transformations, driven by the inherent properties of quantum mechanics. This work presents a preliminary investigation of the feasibility and potential advantages of this approach in tackling complex topological problems.

title: Dynamic Topology Quantum State Compression
abstract: Quantum state compression is a crucial task in quantum information science, aiming to reduce the number of qubits required while maintaining high fidelity. Static compression techniques often struggle with large datasets, necessitating dynamic approaches. This paper proposes a novel dynamic topology-based quantum state compression algorithm, leveraging the inherent properties of topological structures to achieve efficient data transfer. We present a mechanism that dynamically adjusts the topology of the quantum state, enabling targeted compression and optimization. The algorithm's core principle is the creation of a 'dynamic' topology that adapts to the input, resulting in improved compression ratios and reduced computational complexity compared to static methods. This work explores the potential of utilizing topological properties for efficient data manipulation within the quantum realm.

title: 基于动态自适应的动态图论优化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic self-adaptive graph optimization algorithm designed to enhance model performance and accuracy through dynamic structural adjustments. Traditional graph optimization methods often rely on manual design, limiting the algorithm's adaptability. Our approach leverages a "dynamic graph structure" mechanism, continuously adjusting graph parameters based on data feedback and model error. This dynamic adjustment allows the algorithm to automatically refine the graph, mitigating the limitations of static optimization techniques. We present a comprehensive analysis of the algorithm's performance and discuss its potential applications across various modeling domains.

title: Temporal Data Causal Learning and Dynamic Graph Models
abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of causal learning from time-series data, a problem frequently encountered in various domains such as healthcare, finance, and environmental science. Traditional causal inference methods often struggle to capture the dynamic nature inherent in temporal data, leading to inaccurate causal models. This work proposes a novel approach that combines structural causal inference (SCI) with dynamic graph models. The core idea is to learn causal relationships directly from time-series data using SCI and then represent these relationships within a dynamic graph structure that can evolve over time. We define a framework for incorporating temporal dependencies within the causal model, allowing us to represent and reason about dynamic causal pathways. The resulting dynamic graph model can then be used for prediction, intervention analysis, and understanding the underlying causal mechanisms driving the observed temporal patterns. We outline the key components of this framework and discuss its potential applications, highlighting the advantages of this approach over traditional methods. The paper culminates in a conceptual model and provides a foundation for future research in this area.

The paper presents a theoretical framework and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach in addressing challenges encountered in predictive modeling.

title: Formal Semantic Networks: Adaptive Optimization
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to intelligent system development centered around the adaptive optimization of formal semantic networks. The core idea involves leveraging the structural and relational information embedded within semantic networks to automatically generate efficient algorithms and programs. This is achieved by transforming the network into a formal logic representation, utilizing formal reasoning and optimization algorithms to uncover implicit knowledge and hidden relationships. The resulting algorithms and programs then enable the intelligent system to adapt and evolve autonomously. We demonstrate the potential of this methodology to reduce the complexity of artificial intelligence development by automating the process of algorithm design and self-improvement. The primary contribution lies in the integration of formal semantics with algorithmic optimization, leading to a system capable of self-generation and adaptive evolution. This approach aims to provide a framework for building more robust and intelligent systems by directly translating semantic understanding into executable code.

title: Title: Adaptive Graph Neural Network Knowledge Distillation
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive graph neural network (GNN) knowledge distillation method. The core idea is to dynamically adjust the parameters of the GNN to effectively transfer knowledge from a large model to a smaller model, thereby improving model efficiency and generalization ability. We propose a novel approach that incorporates a learning rate schedule for the GNN's parameters, allowing the model to adaptively adjust its structure to better match the target model. The method is evaluated on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in model efficiency and performance compared to existing knowledge distillation techniques.

title: A Novel Computation Architecture Based on Quantum Coherence
abstract: This paper proposes a novel computation architecture centered around the exploitation of quantum coherence. The core concept involves structuring a computational system to leverage the inherent parallelism afforded by quantum coherence, thereby aiming to significantly enhance computational efficiency compared to traditional architectures. We outline a framework where interconnected quantum systems operate in a manner that maximizes the duration of quantum coherence, allowing for parallel processing of multiple computational tasks simultaneously. The architecture is designed to mitigate decoherence effects, a primary challenge in quantum computing, through strategic system design and operational protocols. This approach represents a fundamentally new paradigm in computation, shifting from sequential, deterministic operations to a massively parallel, probabilistic one based on the quantum mechanical principles of superposition and coherence. The potential impact of this architecture extends across various fields, including scientific simulations, optimization problems, and machine learning, where the ability to process vast amounts of data concurrently offers a transformative advantage. ---

title: Leakage-Controlled Classification of Dataset-Derived Ordinal p53-Signature Size Categories in Fallopian-Tube Immunohistochemistry
abstract: Background and Objectives: p53 signatures are segments of strongly p53-immunoreactive secretory epithelium in the fallopian tube. We tested whether fixed pathology-pretrained image representations could classify three ordered categories reconstructed from the public dataset’s reported cell-count intervals. Methods: The primary cohort comprised 113 canonical p53 20× fields from 67 patients: 59 Small (12–20 cells), 24 Medium (21–80), and 30 Large (>80). A 141-field partial-label cohort retained boundary-spanning intervals for sensitivity analysis. Twenty-six eligible feature/head pipelines were evaluated by three-repeat five-fold nested patient-grouped cross-validation. Within every outer fold, the pipeline was selected using inner validation only; primary performance metrics were computed within each repeat and averaged across the three repeats, while the resulting 339 held-out predictions were pooled only for the confusion-matrix visualization. Uncertainty was estimated using 2000 patient-cluster bootstrap replicates conditional on these recorded predictions. Results: The fold-wise nested selector achieved quadratic-weighted kappa (QWK) 0.687 (95% CI 0.547–0.785), macro-F1 0.628 (0.568–0.680), balanced accuracy 0.637 (0.581–0.693), macro-AUROC 0.805 (0.750–0.855), and macro-AUPRC 0.681 (0.633–0.754). title: Anomaly detection in long-term time series with Transformer and variational autoencoder
abstract: Abstract Anomaly detection is crucial for ensuring system reliability and providing early warnings of potential failures. However, long-term time-series anomaly detection remains challenging because anomalous events are rare, anomaly patterns are diverse, and temporal dependencies can extend across multiple scales. Traditional methods and existing deep learning models still struggle to jointly represent fine-grained temporal variation, long-range contextual information, and the distribution of normal patterns. This work presents Transformer with variational autoencoder (TransVAE), a framework that combines a dual-embedding representation pipeline, a Transformer encoder for long-range dependency modeling, and VAE-based latent regularization of encoded features. Specifically, local position-aware embeddings and feature-wise global embeddings are integrated into a shared representation before attention modeling, and the VAE is applied to the Transformer-encoded representation to regularize the latent space of normal patterns. Evaluations on benchmark time-series datasets show that TransVAE outperforms several state-of-the-art baselines, achieving improvements in the area under the receiver operating characteristic by 6.7% and 13.6%, respectively. Ablation and sensitivity analyses further support the contributions of each component of the framework. These results demonstrate that TransVAE provides an effective and robust solution for long-term time-series anomaly detection.

title: EigenLI: Spectral Approximations to Late Interaction
abstract: Late-interaction models such as ColBERT achieve strong effectiveness by representing each document with many token-level vectors, but this expressivity leads to large indexing cost, storage footprints and expensive MaxSim scoring. We show that late-interaction representations exhibit an intrinsic low-rank structure: document token embeddings concentrate in a low-dimensional subspace that preserves most of the retrieval signal. Leveraging this observation, we introduce EigenLI, a spectral approximation framework that compresses late-interaction representations via document-specific low-dimensional subspaces. Unlike clustering or pooling methods, EigenLI identifies the dominant eigendirections of each document and uses them to construct reduced interaction representations. Empirically, $k$-EigenLI with $k \le 32$ outperforms k-means and Ward clustering based pooling methods on ColBERTv2 and AnswerAI-ColBERT-small; GTE-ModernColBERT exhibits a different tradeoff at $k=32$, where clustering methods perform better. The same spectral construction also yields EigenLI-SV, an ANN-compatible single-vector representation derived from the second-order summary of the reduced structure. Across multiple datasets and all three text models, EigenLI-SV consistently outperforms comparable single-vector surrogates such as MUVERA.

title: Robust Decentralized Personalized Federated Learning via Prediction-Constrained Neighborhood Collaboration
abstract: This paper proposes a robust decentralized personalized federated learning method R-DPFL, that enables clients to reduce the impact of Byzantine attacks via robust neighborhood direction estimation and history-based update trend prediction, rather than purely aggregating client models as in the existing work. In R-DPFL, each client first computes the current-round model update by aggregating the received neighborhood update vectors. It then predicts what this update should be based on its historical values and local model changes. Finally, R-DPFL computes the difference between these two quantities, adaptively clips this difference, and adds it to the local update. We prove convergence of the learning process through rigorous analysis and show that honest clients maintain stable personalized descent dynamics under Byzantine neighbor perturbations without requiring consensus among neighboring models. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10 demonstrate that RDPFL consistently outperforms state-of-the-art decentralized and personalized federated learning baselines under heterogeneous and adversarial settings.

title: Progressive Pruning: Analyzing the Impact of Intersection Attacks
abstract: Stream-based communication dominates today's Internet, posing unique challenges for anonymous communication networks (ACNs). Traditionally designed for independent messages, ACNs struggle to account for the inherent vulnerabilities of streams, such as susceptibility to intersection attacks. In this work, we address this gap and introduce progressive pruning, a novel methodology for quantifying the susceptibility to intersection attacks. Progressive pruning quantifies and monitors anonymity sets over time, providing an assessment of an adversary's success in correlating senders and receivers. We leverage this methodology to analyze synthetic scenarios and large-scale simulations of the Tor network using our newly developed TorFS simulator. Our findings reveal that anonymity is significantly influenced by stream length, user population, and stream distribution across the network. These insights highlight critical design challenges for future ACNs seeking to safeguard stream-based communication against traffic analysis attacks.

title: Ontology matching evaluation : A statistical perspective
abstract: This paper proposes statistical approaches to test if the difference between two ontology matchers is real. Specifically, the performances of the matchers over multiple data sets are obtained and based on their performances, the conclusion can be drawn whether one method is better than one another or not. To do so, the paired t-test and Wilcoxon signed rank test are proposed and the comparisons over six recently proposed methods are reported. © 2016, CEUR-WS. All rights reserved.

title: AI元系统原生智能理论
abstract: 当前人工智能研究在语义接地、可解释性及能效方面遭遇根本性瓶颈,其深层根源在于将智能本质等同于高维统计拟合。本文提出元系统原生智能理论(MSɅIT),主张智能并非数据驱动的函数逼近,而是基于”主导-调制”二元操作的代数构造过程,其深层逻辑结构由第一性关系R₀生成,全部推理规则均可还原为R₀的有限次派生操作。 本文的核心贡献在于:(1)从认知发生学的操作闭包原则出发,论证六层基础认知范畴构成认知系统闭环表征的最小完备集合,其二元组合生成64维基础标签空间——64在此被定位为认知智能的必要基元数,而非宇宙的普遍常数;(2)严格定义第一性关系R₀的三层公理(主导约束Dom、调制约束Mod、不可逆约束¬Rev),并论证其在封闭推理系统内的逻辑必然性,同时明确其在开放系统中的弱化条件;(3)构建逻辑模态范畴L与C₅-集合范畴离散单点集骨架子范畴的函子等价,为模态推理提供范畴论的结构支撑;(4)将先验公理体系翻译为”只读定义域-可修改调制域”的分层架构工程规范,实现从形式理论到可执行约束的映射。 本文明确划定理论的适用边界:MSɅIT适用于具有清晰”定义域-调制域”分层的认知系统与AI推理系统,其公理体系在此边界内成立;在开放复杂系统中,¬Rev公理弱化为统计不可逆约束。64维空间的必然性被限定为认知操作闭包的基元数,而非跨越物理-生物-认知所有层级的普适常数。这一边界划定使理论具备清晰的可证伪性。

title: Title: Adaptive Topological Field Theory Quantum Computing Algorithm Design
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum computing algorithm based on Adaptive Topological Field Theory (ATFT). The core idea of the algorithm is to leverage the unique properties of ATFT to enhance the simulation and optimization of quantum computations, thereby improving the efficiency and accuracy of quantum computing. We introduce a framework for dynamically adjusting the parameters of the ATFT to tailor the computational process to specific problems. The algorithm's design incorporates a novel approach to mapping quantum states onto the ATFT landscape, facilitating efficient exploration of the solution space. We explore the potential of this approach for tackling various quantum algorithms, specifically focusing on those benefiting from enhanced simulation capabilities. The research aims to advance the field of quantum computing by providing a practical and efficient method for optimization and simulation.

title: Nonlinear Geometry Topology and Quantum Computing: A Cross-Disciplinary Exploration
abstract: This paper investigates the intersection of nonlinear geometry topology and quantum computing, proposing a novel quantum computation algorithm predicated on a framework rooted in topological quantum information processing. The core claim is the development of an algorithm capable of achieving deeper control and measurement of quantum entanglement through the incorporation of self-linking and self-connectivity properties within a quantum qubit system. This advancement aims to significantly enhance the efficiency and computational capabilities of quantum computing by leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. The work presents a mechanism for establishing a quantum qubit system structured by topological principles, enabling enhanced entanglement manipulation and utilizing self-association properties to guide quantum computation. The investigation explores the potential for this approach to represent a significant shift in quantum algorithm design, moving beyond the limitations of classical qubit operations.

title: Dynamic Semantic Network Reasoning Engine (DSNRE)
abstract: This paper introduces the Dynamic Semantic Network Reasoning Engine (DSNRE), a novel approach to knowledge graph reasoning that addresses the limitations of traditional, static systems. The core claim is that integrating continuous, active semantic understanding modeling with knowledge graph inference processes enables adaptive, dynamic reasoning in response to evolving data and context. DSNRE employs a multi-layered feedback loop system comprised of a rule-based and probabilistic graph inference engine, a pre-trained language model-based semantic understanding module, an active query generation module, and a continuous learning module. The system iteratively refines its understanding and reasoning capabilities through proactive querying and continuous learning, achieving real-time adaptation to dynamic semantic changes. The key innovation lies in the deep integration of semantic understanding and inference, moving beyond static knowledge-based deduction to a more intelligent, self-aware system. This paper outlines the architecture, functionality, and theoretical underpinnings of DSNRE, highlighting its potential for applications requiring robust and adaptable reasoning in dynamic environments.

title: Nonlinear Topological Quantum Computing Adaptive Learning Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel adaptive learning algorithm for nonlinear topological quantum computing (NTQC) based on self-organized quantum systems. Traditional machine learning approaches rely on pre-defined models, while this algorithm leverages the inherent adaptability of non-linear topological quantum systems. The core mechanism involves dynamically adjusting quantum system parameters to optimize performance in response to environmental changes. This approach offers enhanced scalability, flexibility, and potential for efficient quantum computation. We present a theoretical framework and initial implementation demonstrating the algorithm's capabilities in a simplified model. The paper concludes with a discussion of the challenges and future directions for this research.

title: 基于非对称性约束的概率图的自适应优化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm for probabilistic graphs that leverages non-symmetry constraints to dynamically adjust graph structure, ensuring stability in optimization results. Traditional optimization methods often require manual design of the graph structure, which struggles to adapt to dynamic graph changes. This algorithm utilizes non-symmetry constraints to transform the optimization problem into a dynamic probability graph structure, enabling a more flexible and robust optimization process. The core mechanism involves iteratively refining the graph structure based on the input probability distribution, resulting in improved convergence and stability. This work presents a framework for adapting optimization algorithms to complex probabilistic graph environments.

title: Quantum Decoherence Control Theory
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Quantum Decoherence Control Theory aimed at enhancing coherence times in quantum states through precise environmental noise management. The core mechanism relies on analyzing the impact of environmental noise on quantum states, utilizing quantum information theory and noise theory foundations to design targeted control strategies. Specifically, the theory proposes feedback control and quantum error correction techniques to suppress noise propagation and extend coherence times. Unlike existing approaches primarily relying on physical shielding and quantum error correction, this theory offers a more granular and adaptable method for mitigating decoherence, representing a significant advancement in quantum information processing. The theoretical framework is presented, outlining key equations and control parameters, and demonstrating the potential for achieving significantly longer coherence times under controlled noise conditions. This work lays the groundwork for future research into practical implementations of this theory.

title: Quantum Adaptive Topology Optimization (QATO)
abstract: Quantum Adaptive Topology Optimization (QATO) is a novel optimization algorithm designed to leverage quantum self-adaptation principles to enhance the performance of quantum systems. This paper introduces a QATO algorithm that dynamically adjusts parameters within a quantum system to achieve optimal results, offering a significant departure from traditional optimization techniques. We detail the core mechanism, exploring how the quantum self-adaptation allows for the exploration of complex, multi-scale optimization landscapes, ultimately leading to improved system performance. The paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the algorithm's design, demonstrating its effectiveness through theoretical analysis and experimental validation. The primary goal is to provide a robust and efficient method for optimizing quantum systems, potentially unlocking new capabilities and applications.

title: Meta-Learning for Hyperparameter Optimization
abstract: Hyperparameter optimization (HPO) is a critical but often time-consuming step in the machine learning pipeline. Traditional methods like grid search and random search are inefficient, particularly for complex models and large search spaces. This paper investigates the application of meta-learning techniques to address the challenges of HPO. We propose a framework where HPO is formulated as a meta-learning problem, leveraging past optimization experiences to accelerate the learning process. Our approach aims to learn a meta-learner that can rapidly adapt to new model-dataset combinations, significantly reducing the HPO time. We demonstrate that meta-learning can effectively learn optimal hyperparameter configurations, leading to improved model performance compared to conventional HPO methods. The core claim is that meta-learning provides a mechanism for rapid and efficient hyperparameter tuning. The key mechanism is framing HPO as a learning problem and using meta-learning algorithms for training.

abstract: This paper investigates the potential of dynamic topology extension in probability space logic to enhance data analysis and machine learning algorithms, particularly concerning high-dimensional datasets. This approach promises to overcome the limitations of static logic systems in effectively processing high-dimensional data. The investigation focuses on the advantages and challenges of this dynamic topology approach, highlighting its potential impact on algorithm efficiency and data representation.

abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum mechanics to revolutionize particle trajectory optimization. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with dynamic constraints, hindering efficient trajectory design. We introduce a novel approach that leverages quantum algorithms to dynamically adjust constraints based on the particle's behavior, mimicking the adaptive mechanisms observed in biological systems. This integration of quantum principles offers a significant leap forward in optimizing particle trajectories, achieving enhanced performance and adaptability compared to traditional methods. The paper details the proposed methodology, including the quantum algorithm framework and a preliminary analysis of its effectiveness.

title: 可解释人工智能的因果推断引擎
abstract: This paper proposes a novel engine for Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) focused on causal inference. The core claim is to construct an AI engine capable of performing causal reasoning and providing more reliable explanations for decision-making. The engine leverages a mechanism based on structural causal models, integrating Bayesian Networks and Deep Learning to identify and infer causal relationships, ultimately generating explainable decision processes. Traditional XAI methods often struggle to provide genuine causal explanations, limiting their utility in high-stakes decision scenarios. This work addresses this limitation by explicitly incorporating causal inference, significantly enhancing the reliability and trustworthiness of AI-driven decisions. The proposed system aims to move beyond simply explaining correlations to elucidating the underlying causal mechanisms driving outcomes. The system is designed to be modular and adaptable, allowing for the integration of diverse datasets and causal discovery techniques. Further research will focus on refining the explanation generation process and validating the engine's performance across various domains.

title: The Great Amnesia: AI Agent Memory as the Binding Constraint on Autonomous Systems in Enterprise and Defense
abstract: Every frontier laboratory is racing to make the system smarter. None is racing to make it remember. That is not a gap in the market. That is the market. Four years of capability gains have not moved the rate at which organisations put artificial intelligence into production. The industry reads that as an adoption problem. It is an architecture problem, and the evidence is already public. A frontier laboratory's own usage data shows computer and mathematical tasks at roughly 35 percent of consumer conversations and close to 44 percent of API traffic, with software error correction the single most frequent task: the most capable reasoning systems ever built, deployed overwhelmingly on work small enough to fit inside one session. Enterprise research puts pilot failure at approximately 95 percent and attributes it not to model quality but to a learning gap. Time-horizon measurement shows 50 percent horizons in hours against 80 percent horizons of roughly one. And long-horizon agent performance collapses from 40 to 50 percent down to below 10 percent when the same task is embedded in a longer history, with the required information still inside the context window. That last result settles the question. Not knowledge, not retrieval, not context length. Capability is compounding and continuity is not, and no quantity of parameters has ever fixed an architecture problem. The paper maps where every layer of the market sits relative to that gap, including Palantir, Anduril and Shield AI, shows defense buying the identical defect at scale, demonstrates why memory features, larger windows and retrieval each fail to close it, specifies the eight properties a continuity layer must hold, and issues an open two-cycle test that any laboratory, platform, prime or programme office can run against its own stack, and against the author's. Version 2.0 supersedes version 1.0. Companion preprint: Continuous Mission Intelligence: The Decisive Architecture for Command at Machine Speed, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22646255. The author is co-founder and Chief Executive Officer of Rebootix AI, Inc.

title: Adaptive Encryption Framework for Web Applications: A Risk-Based Approach to Dynamic Algorithm Selection
abstract: Web applications increasingly handle sensitive data in diverse use cases, but conventional encryption implementations apply a uniform level of cryptographic protection to all traffic, regardless of the associated risk. This static approach results in either excessive computational overhead when applying maximum encryption universally, or inadequate protection when using lightweight encryption to preserve performance. This paper proposes an Adaptive Encryption Framework (AEF) designed to bridge the gap between performance and security in web applications. Rather than relying on a static protocol, AEF dynamically adjusts encryption algorithms based on a real-time composite risk score (0–100). This score is derived from six weighted variables: network risk (25%), authentication strength (20%), behavioral risk (20%), device trust (15%), data sensitivity (15%), and temporal risk (5%). Depending on the calculated risk, the system automatically transitions between three distinct security tiers: GREEN (utilizing ChaCha20-Poly1305), YELLOW (AES-256-GCM), or RED (AES-256-GCM with per-request HKDF key derivation for key isolation). All three profiles use exclusively standardized cryptographic primitives. The proposed weighting distribution was evaluated through sensitivity analysis on 27 framework-executed scenarios and further calibrated using 40,000 labeled application requests. Within these experimental conditions, it achieved complete agreement with the expected scenario classifications, and no alternative weight configuration produced better held-out performance. Additional validation on 61,065 HTTP requests from the CSIC 2010 dataset yielded an area under the ROC curve (ROC AUC) of 0.860, with no attack request assigned to the lightweight profile under the evaluated operating conditions. Across three hardware platforms and four payload sizes, all encryption profiles maintained sub-millisecond latency. Extended load testing showed that a four-worker Node.js cluster sustained 4948 requests per second at 2000 concurrent connections, a 7.1-fold improvement over a single process. When hardware cryptographic acceleration was disabled, ChaCha20-Poly1305 became up to 9.1 times faster than AES-256-GCM, supporting its use as the lightweight profile. The framework proposed in this paper operationalizes the qualitative risk assessment guidelines from NIST SP 800-30 and SP 800-63 into a quantitative, automated encryption selection mechanism for web applications, evaluated under the hardware platforms, concurrency levels and traffic assumptions described in this study.

title: Dynamic obstacle avoidance method for 3D animation group based on multi-agent reinforcement learning
abstract: At the forefront of 3D animation, virtual reality and robotics, it is difficult to realistically and efficiently simulate the group behavior of a large number of people and objects. Previously, traditional rule-based or optimization-based methods often encountered critical problems such as local collisions, unnatural trajectories, or the inability to escape deadlocks—especially in complex, high-density, and dynamic environments. In addition, these old methods also have limitations in overall coordination and flexibility, as they typically rely on local optimal calculations that fail to account for global group dynamics, inevitably leading to deadlocks in high-density continuous control scenarios. To tackle these specific limitations, our proposed approach integrates a localized attention mechanism. By supplying the transformer encoding into a policy network, each “agent” effectively collects and filters information about nearby agents and dynamic obstacles, proactively anticipating collision threats to maintain global coordination. It is noteworthy that the proposed method utilizes a comprehensive reward function that balances obstacle avoidance, movement efficiency, and path fluency. We have fully tested this method called Attention-MAPPO for populations with low/high density, static/dynamic barriers in the Unity 3D modeling environment. The experimental results show that the average obstacle avoidance success rate of this method in all tasks is 92.6%, and the average movement time is 12.4 s. Compared with the baseline standard MAPPO, its success rate has increased by an average of 4.4%, and the average movement time has been shortened by 6.8%, showing significant performance improvement. Furthermore, ablation studies on the attention mechanism clearly demonstrate its crucial role in achieving optimal performance in highly complex dynamic environments. This study provides a powerful and scalable solution for a real, effective team simulation that has a big impact on interactive virtual environments, game development and intelligent robots.

title: Learning to Fly: Stable Vision-Guided UAV Servoing with Compact Target-Centric Cues and Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Vision-guided reinforcement learning for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) remains challenging due to unstable policy optimisation, aggressive exploration, and the cost of high-dimensional visual perception. In this work, we investigate long-horizon UAV visual servoing using compact target-centric cues combined with low-dimensional sensor measurements. Rather than learning directly from RGB images, lightweight target segmentation provides image-space offsets and relative depth, which are combined with quadrotor velocity and projected-gravity measurements into a compact 12D policy observation. We compare Direct PPO with three matched-budget curriculum strategies: a Visual curriculum that progressively expands target placement difficulty, a Dynamics curriculum that gradually relaxes action constraints and smoothing, and a Joint curriculum that combines both progressions. All strategies reach comparable nominal performance, with complementary advantages across tracking metrics. Observation ablations show that proprioceptive measurements are critical for stable flight and image-space cues for target alignment, while explicit depth is not necessary for strong performance in the evaluated setting. Against tuned classical visual-servo controllers, learned policies show greater robustness to strong control and visual perturbations, while the Visual curriculum exhibits the smallest degradation under unseen target motion. Overall, the results demonstrate that compact target-centric representations can support robust long-horizon aerial visual servoing and that visual curriculum training can improve robustness to dynamic distribution shifts despite limited gains in nominal performance.

title: Quantum Approximate Counting with Bernoulli Oracles
abstract: Quantum counting is a fundamental quantum algorithm that estimates the fraction of marked elements using a membership oracle, achieving a quadratic speedup over classical sampling. The membership oracle, however, assumes exact labeling of each element, but this assumption fails when the labels are inherently probabilistic. We study quantum counting with \emph{Bernoulli oracles}, where given $m$ Bernoulli distributions with unknown biases $p_1,\dots,p_m$ and a gap parameter $Δ$, the goal is to estimate the fraction $ρ$ of \emph{positive} distributions ($p_i\ge1/2+Δ$) to within additive error $ε$. We prove an upper bound of $\tilde{O}\!\big(\frac{\sqrtρ}{Δε}+\frac{1}{Δ\sqrtε}\big)$ queries, achieving a quadratic speedup over the classical sample complexity. % of $Θ(ρ/Δ^2ε^2)$. Our algorithm first uses the Quantum Singular Value Transformation (QSVT) to coherently amplify the bias gap without collapsing the superposition over distributions, and then applies two-stage adaptive amplitude estimation. We complement this upper bound with a near-matching lower bound of $Ω(\sqrtρ/(Δε))$ via a new composition theorem for the quantum adversary method in the Boolean-over-average-case direction. For the special case of a constant gap $Δ=Θ(1)$, which corresponds to the bounded-error oracle where each query returns the correct label with constant probability, our bounds specialize to $\tilde{O}\big(\frac{\sqrtρ}ε+\frac{1}{\sqrtε}\big)$ and $Ω(\frac{\sqrtρ}ε)$, thereby characterizing the query complexity of quantum counting with bounded-error oracles.

title: Trust-But-Verify: Poisoning-Resilient Locally Private Graph Learning Protocols
abstract: Built upon local differential privacy (LDP), locally private graph learning protocols have emerged as an important paradigm for decentralized graph learning, balancing privacy protection and learning utility. Under such protocols, each user locally perturbs their node features and adjacency information before transmission, ensuring formal privacy guarantees without original data leaving the device. However, the inherently open participation nature renders these protocols critically vulnerable to data poisoning attacks, where adversaries inject carefully crafted malicious nodes to corrupt neighborhood aggregation and degrade downstream utility. Despite the severity of this threat, effective defenses in this setting remain largely unexplored. In this paper, we propose VERITAS, a poisoning-resilient locally private graph learning protocol built on a trust-but-verify paradigm. By introducing a verification list encoding graded peer trust levels, VERITAS jointly privatizes node features and graph structure on the user side, while exploiting bilateral attestation asymmetry on the server side to identify and prune malicious nodes. Concretely, VERITAS comprises four synergistic stages: (1) local data perturbation, (2) attestation-driven malicious node pruning, (3) utility restoration via dual denoising, and (4) robust private graph learning. Extensive experiments on four real-world benchmark datasets across multiple LDP mechanisms and GNN architectures demonstrate that VERITAS effectively defends against data poisoning attacks and significantly improves downstream graph learning utility under rigorous privacy guarantees.

title: Measuring Prompt-Induced Instability in Large Language Model–Based Fact Verification.
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to verify factual claims, yet the stability of their verdicts is rarely examined. We ask whether an LLM returns the same fact-verification label for the same claim when only the prompt phrasing changes, or even when nothing changes across identical repeated runs. We evaluate three frontier models (GPT-5.6, Claude Opus 4.8, and Gemini 3.1 Pro) on 250 label-balanced FEVER claims, presented without evidence, under five semantically distinct prompt framings, each repeated five times, for a total of 18,750 predictions. Using paired statistics (paired bootstrap, exact McNemar) and bootstrap confidence intervals, we find that verdicts are not reproducible even at temperature 0 (86.7-93.3% determinism), that models differ significantly in stability, and that instability concentrates on the abstention (NOT ENOUGH INFO) decision rather than on factual reversals. We argue that stability must be reported alongside accuracy when evaluating LLM fact-checkers.
