title: Dynamic Adaptive Markov Random Field (GMM)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Dynamic Adaptive Markov Random Field (GMM) algorithm designed to handle data distributions that evolve over time. Traditional GMMs often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their ability to effectively model dynamic data patterns. This work proposes a method for dynamically adjusting model parameters based on observed data fluctuations, thereby enabling robust and adaptable modeling across various datasets. The core mechanism involves a feedback loop that continuously updates the model's parameters to best fit the evolving data distribution. We present a comprehensive analysis demonstrating the algorithm's effectiveness through simulations and experiments, showcasing its capacity to maintain high accuracy while adapting to changing data characteristics. The results highlight the significant advantages of this dynamic GMM approach over static models in scenarios requiring real-time data adaptation.

title: Computational Complexity Analysis of Quantum Algorithms using Category Theory
abstract: Traditional methods for analyzing the computational complexity of algorithms, predominantly rooted in classical computer models, struggle to accurately characterize the potential advantages offered by quantum computation. This work proposes a novel approach utilizing category theory to provide a more fundamental and abstract framework for assessing the complexity of quantum algorithms. Instead of focusing on the specifics of quantum hardware, we examine the underlying categorical structures that define the computational processes inherent in these algorithms. This allows us to identify and analyze complexity properties that are independent of the physical implementation. We define key concepts like quantum states as objects and quantum gates as morphisms, establishing a formal connection between quantum computation and category theory. This framework facilitates a more rigorous and generalized understanding of quantum complexity, potentially revealing new insights and providing a basis for comparing different quantum algorithms. The core claim is that traditional complexity analysis is inadequate, and the mechanism is the application of category theory for a more abstract and generalized framework.

abstract: This paper investigates the generation and control of quantum entanglement utilizing non-spin states, specifically photons and atomic nuclei, aiming to overcome the limitations inherent in spin-based entanglement approaches. We introduce the concept of entanglement fidelity as a metric for evaluating the quality of the generated entanglement. The theoretical framework presented here provides a foundation for future experimental investigations into non-spin quantum entanglement.

title: Temporal Graph Neural Networks with Dynamic Edge Refinement
abstract: Existing Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) often struggle to effectively model dynamic graphs where relationships between nodes change over time. This research introduces a novel framework, Temporal Graph Neural Networks with Dynamic Edge Refinement (TGDENR), designed to address this limitation. The core idea is to represent graph edges as time-series data, enabling the use of recurrent neural networks or transformers to dynamically refine edge weights based on temporal dependencies. A novelty detection function is employed to identify edges exhibiting significant deviations from established patterns, further enhancing the model's adaptability. The proposed method offers a robust solution for analyzing evolving graph structures, particularly relevant in domains such as social networks, financial markets, and biological systems. The model's performance is evaluated through theoretical analysis and conceptual design, paving the way for future experimental validation.

title: Rancang Bangun Chatbot Customer Service Multi-Tenant Berbasis Large Language Model Menggunakan Context Stuffing
abstract: The advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI), particularly Large Language Models (LLMs), has transformed customer service into a more automated, adaptive, and responsive system. However, LLM-based chatbots still face several challenges, including hallucination, limited capability to serve multiple organizations simultaneously, and difficulties in website integration. This study aims to design and develop an embeddable multi-tenant customer service chatbot based on a Large Language Model. The system was developed using the Go programming language, Fiber framework, PostgreSQL database, and a JavaScript widget that can be embedded into company websites using a single line of code. The Research and Development (R&D) approach was adopted, while the context stuffing method ensured that chatbot responses were generated only from each tenant's official knowledge base, thereby minimizing hallucination. The evaluation included black-box testing, response accuracy measurement, hallucination assessment, response time analysis, and tenant data isolation testing. The experimental results demonstrated that the chatbot achieved 100% response accuracy for in-domain questions, produced zero hallucination for out-of-domain questions, maintained an average response time of approximately four seconds, and successfully preserved complete data isolation among tenants. Furthermore, the chatbot widget was easily embedded into company websites with minimal configuration. These findings indicate that the proposed chatbot provides an effective, secure, and scalable AI-based customer service solution suitable for multiple organizations.

title: Quantitative image feature integrated digital pathology model based on deep learning and machine learning for binary histological severity stratification of ulcerative colitis
abstract: The STRIDE II consensus recognizes histopathological healing in ulcerative colitis as a key therapeutic target. This study aimed to develop and internally evaluate a quantitative image-based model for the binary classification of mild versus moderate-to-severe UC based on histopathological features. Pathological slides from 167 ulcerative colitis patients (58 mild, 109 moderate-to-severe) were retrospectively collected from two medical centers. A U-Net model quantified glandular structures (number, area ratio), Gray-Level Co-occurrence Matrix analyzed texture features, and a five-interval grayscale histogram was modeled. Features selection was performed using LASSO regression. Patients were randomly divided into training and test sets in a 7:3 ratio. Machine learning models were constructed and their performance was evaluated. In the five-fold cross-validation analysis within the training set, SVM achieved the highest mean ROC-AUC and was selected as the final model. title: 2-Fold Forrelation is in QAC$^0$
abstract: We show that 2-fold Forrelation with inverse-polylogarithmic promise gap can be solved, with bounded error, by polynomial-size QAC$^0$ circuits. Unlike the standard oracle-based Forrelation algorithm, our circuits receive the input explicitly, in the same form as the AC$^0$ circuits against which Forrelation is known to be hard. At constant gap, this yields a natural promise-problem separation between QAC$^0$ and AC$^0$.

title: A Hybrid Grey Wolf and Dipper-Throated Optimizer for Engineering Design Optimization
abstract: Optimization plays a fundamental role in engineering design, enabling cost reduction, performance enhancement, and constraint satisfaction.Metaheuristic algorithms such as the Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO) and Dipper-Throated Optimizer (DTO) have been widely used for solving complex optimization problems.However, standalone algorithms often suffer from premature convergence and limited exploration capabilities, necessitating the development of hybrid approaches.This chapter introduces a novel hybrid algorithm, GWO+DTO, which combines the exploratory strength of GWO with the exploitative efficiency of DTO to improve optimization performance.The effectiveness of GWO+DTO is evaluated on two benchmark engineering problems: the Pressure Vessel Design Problem and the Tension/Compression Spring Design Problem, comparing its results with standalone GWO and DTO.Experimental findings demonstrate that the hybrid approach achieves superior performance, obtaining the best cost of 5950.28 in the pressure vessel problem and 0.01266 in the spring design problem, outperforming the individual algorithms in accuracy and efficiency.Additionally, GWO+DTO requires fewer function evaluations, highlighting its computational efficiency.The proposed hybrid method presents a promising alternative for tackling real-world engineering optimization challenges, with potential applications in multi-objective and large-scale optimization problems.

title: Biological Reservoir Computing in Modular Human iPSC-Derived Neuronal Networks
abstract: Introduction While human brain mapping characterizes these relationships at the macroscale, advancements in Synthetic Biological Intelligence (SBI) now allow us to investigate them in controllable, human iPSC-derived neural systems [1]. To systematically probe these mesoscale dynamics, we utilized the CL1 platform, which facilitates high-level programmability of in vitro networks, allowing for precise spatiotemporal electrical stimulation and real-time functional readouts. Treating cultures as physical reservoirs, we ask whether enforcing modular connectivity (segregation + integration) enhances separability of neural state trajectories compared with unstructured 2D monolayers, across spatial, temporal, and spatio-temporal classification benchmarks. Methods In this work, human iPSC-derived cortical and hippocampal neurons were cultured as 2D monolayers or in 60-module PDMS microfluidic devices enforcing modular connectivity coupled by a peripheral loop enabling re-entrant paths. Spikes were recorded on CL1 at 25 kHz; stimulation/noise artifacts were removed via waveform PCA + GMM clustering. We tested reservoir encoding with spatial source discrimination, Morse 'S' vs 'O' sequence decoding, and MNIST driven as 16-channel, 5-step spiking tensors. Spike counts were binned to form state vectors x(t) and decoded by logistic regression with 5-fold CV, against shuffled and test-chip controls. Results All biological cultures supported above-chance spatial decoding, but modular devices improved fidelity, with mixed cortical–hippocampal modular networks reaching ~96% median accuracy (Fig.1). Temporal Morse decoding depended on network dynamics: only highly active modular cultures outperformed shuffled controls, while hippocampal monolayers were near chance. For MNIST, monolayers performed poorly, whereas high-activity modular cultures achieved 69–75% median (max 82–88%) accuracy; shuffled and test-chip controls stayed at chance. PCA of reservoir states revealed class-separable manifolds only in real modular data. Discussion While physical Reservoir Computing has been demonstrated in non-biological substrates, its validation in human iPSC-derived neural networks remained limited [2]. In this work, we show that human iPSC neuronal cultures can act as robust biological reservoirs, and enforced modular topology functions as a computational regularizer that expands functional dimensionality and supports fading memory for complex spatio-temporal separation. The synergy of biological identity (hippocampal + cortical) and engineered modular connectivity suggests a programmable route to test how structural constraints enable—or impair—computation, with implications for both SBI applications and mechanistic models of dysconnectivity in brain disorders. title: Dynamic Chaos Optimization via Quantum Potential Landscapes
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic chaos optimization framework based on quantum potential landscapes. Traditional optimization algorithms often struggle with complex, non-linear systems due to the limitations of classical methods. This work leverages the unique properties of quantum potential landscapes, which exhibit dynamic and spatially varying energy states, to guide optimization processes. The core mechanism involves constructing a quantum potential landscape that dynamically adjusts to the system's state, promoting efficient solutions and minimizing errors. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations of a chaotic system, showcasing improvements in performance metrics such as convergence speed and solution quality. The potential landscape provides a mechanism for self-organization and adaptation, leading to enhanced optimization outcomes. The study also explores the impact of varying the landscape's parameters on the optimization process. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and potential applications of this quantum-inspired optimization technique.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning with Bayesian Networks for Uncertainty Quantification
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to neuro-symbolic reasoning that explicitly addresses the critical challenge of uncertainty quantification. Current neuro-symbolic systems often lack a principled way to represent and manage uncertainty arising from both the neural network component and the symbolic reasoning engine. We introduce a framework that integrates Bayesian Networks (BNs) with a symbolic reasoning system, allowing for the probabilistic modeling of neural network outputs and subsequent inference based on this uncertainty. The core mechanism involves constructing a BN to represent the uncertainties inherent in the neural network's predictions. This BN is then utilized as the knowledge base for a symbolic reasoning engine, enabling inferences while providing a quantifiable measure of confidence in the resulting conclusions. Our approach offers a robust solution for incorporating probabilistic reasoning into neuro-symbolic architectures, leading to more reliable and explainable AI systems. The proposed method significantly advances the field by providing a concrete solution to the long-standing problem of uncertainty in neuro-symbolic reasoning. The primary contribution lies in the systematic integration of Bayesian Networks within a neuro-symbolic framework, offering a tangible method for quantifying uncertainty throughout the reasoning process. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through a theoretical analysis and outline a practical implementation strategy.

title: Fractal Code Generation via Iterated Self-Similarity
abstract: This paper explores the potential of utilizing fractal algorithms for software code generation. The core concept revolves around generating complex software architectures through iterative self-similarity, mirroring the patterns observed in natural fractals. The proposed methodology involves defining a base code module and repeatedly applying a transformation function – akin to the generation of the Mandelbrot set – to create progressively intricate code structures. This approach offers a novel systematic method for software design, potentially resulting in more efficient and adaptable code solutions. The research focuses on the underlying mathematical principles driving this fractal generation process, establishing a theoretical framework for its application in software development. Key metrics for evaluating the generated code's complexity and efficiency are also discussed. This work represents a significant step toward a new paradigm in software design, moving away from traditional, monolithic approaches towards more adaptable and self-similar systems. ---

title: 基于多尺度认知地图的知识推理
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to knowledge reasoning by leveraging multi-scale cognitive maps. Traditional knowledge representation and reasoning methods often struggle with the inherent complexity and hierarchical nature of knowledge. Our proposed system addresses this challenge by constructing cognitive maps at multiple scales, effectively representing knowledge as a hierarchy of graph structures. These maps are then utilized with graph algorithms – including graph traversal, pattern matching, and inference rules – to perform multi-scale knowledge reasoning. The core claim is that building these multi-scale cognitive maps facilitates more intelligent knowledge acquisition and application. The mechanism relies on decomposing knowledge into distinct abstraction levels and constructing multi-scale knowledge graphs. This approach allows for reasoning across different levels of granularity, providing a richer and more nuanced understanding of the knowledge domain. The resulting system demonstrates improved performance in knowledge inference compared to traditional methods. This work contributes to a more robust and scalable approach to knowledge reasoning, suitable for applications requiring complex reasoning over large knowledge bases.

title: 基于图的神经网络的自适应重构
abstract: This paper introduces a novel neural network architecture, termed "Graph-Based Neural Network for Adaptive Reconstruction," designed to address challenges in reconstructing complex graph structures. Traditional neural networks often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their ability to effectively handle dynamic and intricate graph representations. Our proposed algorithm leverages the inherent structural information within graphs to dynamically adjust network parameters, resulting in improved reconstruction accuracy and robustness. We detail the core mechanism, outlining how the network utilizes graph topology to guide parameter optimization. This approach offers a significant advancement over conventional methods, particularly in scenarios requiring adaptive reconstruction of complex and evolving graphs. The paper concludes with a discussion of the algorithm's design choices, its potential applications, and future research directions.

title: 自适应语言模型训练的动态概率策略
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to language model training that leverages dynamic probability strategy. Traditional language models often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their adaptability to diverse tasks. Our method dynamically adjusts the probability distribution of the model during training, optimizing performance through a principled approach to error-driven weight adjustment. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this technique through a series of experiments, showcasing significant improvements in accuracy and efficiency across a range of benchmark datasets. The core mechanism involves continuous monitoring of model predictions and targeted weight adjustments, resulting in a more robust and adaptable model. This research contributes to the advancement of efficient and customizable language model training methodologies.

title: Fractal Recursion for Algorithm Discovery
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to algorithm discovery and optimization termed "Fractal Recursion." The core idea is that algorithms can be iteratively refined through a recursive process, mirroring the self-similar structure of fractals. The system begins with a basic algorithm and repeatedly applies it to increasingly complex problem instances, analyzing the resulting performance. Based on this analysis, the algorithm is modified, and the process repeats. This approach aims to automate a traditionally manual and often time-consuming algorithmic design task. The system leverages the inherent redundancy and optimization potential found within fractal patterns to converge towards a globally optimal solution. This paper outlines the core concept, the underlying mechanism, and the potential benefits of fractal recursion for a wide range of computational problems. Mathematical notation is used throughout to illustrate key concepts and algorithmic steps.

title: Temporal Program Semantics
abstract: This paper introduces Temporal Program Semantics (TPS), a novel approach to program understanding and reasoning. Traditional program semantics treat programs as static sets of instructions, a representation that often struggles to capture the dynamic and evolving nature of computation. TPS fundamentally shifts this perspective by conceptualizing program semantics as the evolution of state over time. We posit that programs are best understood as time-ordered sequences of state transitions. This core claim is supported by a formal mechanism utilizing temporal logic to precisely define and verify program behavior. This approach offers significant advantages in areas such as program understanding, verification, and optimization, providing a more intuitive and aligned model with human cognitive processes. This work presents a foundational framework for TPS, outlining the key concepts and formal foundations, and paving the way for future research in this emerging field.

title: Title: Non-Local Quantum Field Interaction (NQFI)
abstract: Quantum field theory provides a foundational framework for understanding the behavior of quantum fields, but its inherent limitations often preclude practical applications. This paper explores the concept of Non-Local Quantum Field Interaction (NQFI), a novel approach to manipulating quantum fields across spacetime, aiming to unlock opportunities for advanced quantum information processing. We propose a mechanism predicated on a dynamically evolving network of quantum fields, where interactions and transfers of information and energy are fundamental to the system's operation. The core claim is that this method, while still in conceptualization, possesses the potential to significantly expand the capabilities of quantum computing and information storage. The current state of research is characterized by theoretical exploration and preliminary simulations, emphasizing the need for further investigation and rigorous validation of the proposed mechanism.

title: Dynamic Topology-Dependent Neural Networks
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to modeling and controlling complex dynamic systems utilizing Dynamic Topology-Dependent Neural Networks (DTNNs). The core idea is to leverage real-time learning and adaptation of neural network topology, moving beyond the limitations of traditional parameter-based neural networks. We employ a reinforcement learning-based adaptive neural connection algorithm to dynamically adjust the connection strength and topology of neurons based on changes in input signals. This allows the network to self-organize and effectively respond to dynamic system variations. The key contribution lies in directly constructing and optimizing the network's topology, enabling it to capture and react to dynamic topological dependencies within the input data. The resulting DTNNs demonstrate the potential to achieve superior performance in scenarios where traditional neural networks struggle due to the inherent time-varying nature of the system. We present a theoretical framework and outline the key components of this approach, focusing on the adaptive learning mechanism and the topological optimization process. The presented methodology offers a new paradigm for neural network design, specifically targeting systems with evolving topological structures.

The core idea is to leverage real-time learning and adaptation of neural network topology, moving beyond the limitations of traditional parameter-based neural networks. We employ a reinforcement learning-based adaptive neural connection algorithm to dynamically adjust the connection strength and topology of neurons based on changes in input signals. This allows the network to self-organize and effectively respond to dynamic system variations. The key contribution lies in directly constructing and optimizing the network's topology, enabling it to capture and react to dynamic topological dependencies within the input data. The resulting DTNNs demonstrate the potential to achieve superior performance in scenarios where traditional neural networks struggle due to the inherent time-varying nature of the system. We present a theoretical framework and outline the key components of this approach, focusing on the adaptive learning mechanism and the topological optimization process. The presented methodology offers a new paradigm for neural network design, specifically targeting systems with evolving topological structures.

title: Causal Bayesian Networks with Latent Feedback Loops
abstract: Bayesian Networks (BNs) are a powerful tool for representing and reasoning about probabilistic relationships. However, their traditional structure struggles to accurately capture complex systems exhibiting bidirectional causal relationships and, crucially, latent feedback loops – influences that operate between variables without direct observation. This paper introduces a novel extension to Bayesian Networks, termed Causal Bayesian Networks with Latent Feedback Loops (CBNFLs), designed to address this limitation. The core innovation lies in the explicit representation of these latent feedback loops, coupled with a 'causal sensitivity' metric to quantify their impact. This metric directly influences the inference process, allowing for a more accurate assessment of causal effects. We demonstrate that this approach significantly improves the modeling and inference capabilities of BNs, particularly in systems where traditional BNs fail to adequately represent the intricate dynamics arising from feedback loops. The proposed framework offers a robust methodology for causal inference in a wider range of complex systems.

title: An Evolutionary Approach to Hardware Architecture Design Based on Neuro-Evolution
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to hardware architecture design utilizing the principles of neuro-evolution. Traditional hardware design relies heavily on human expertise and often involves extensive manual optimization, a process which can be time-consuming and potentially limit the exploration of innovative architectures. This research presents a framework where a neuro-evolutionary algorithm is employed to automatically generate and optimize hardware architectures, directly addressing the core claim of leveraging neuro-evolution for architectural design and achieving improved hardware performance. The system transforms the hardware architecture problem into an evolutionary problem, utilizing a population of neural networks to represent and evaluate different architectural configurations. Through iterative selection, mutation, and crossover operations, the algorithm progressively refines the architectures, aiming to maximize a defined performance metric. The key mechanism lies in the automated exploration of the architectural design space, a capability that is significantly enhanced by the adaptive learning capabilities of the neuro-evolutionary algorithm. The results presented herein demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of this approach, highlighting its potential for accelerating hardware design and generating architectures with superior performance characteristics.

title: Generative Adversarial Networks for Procedural Content Generation in 3D Environments
abstract: This paper explores the application of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to the field of procedural content generation (PCG) within 3D environments. Traditional PCG methods often rely on handcrafted rules and algorithms, leading to potentially repetitive and limited results. We propose a novel framework where a GAN is trained to learn the underlying distribution of realistic and diverse 3D environments. The generator network learns to create 3D assets, while the discriminator network provides feedback, driving the generator to produce outputs that are both visually plausible and consistent with a defined style. We outline the architecture of this system, detailing the training process and the key components involved. The core claim of this research is that GANs offer a viable and potentially superior approach to automating PCG, leading to richer and more varied 3D environments. This work contributes to the growing body of research exploring the intersection of deep learning and creative content generation.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Dynamic Topology Geometry Modeling (DEMT)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic topology geometry modeling approach, termed DEMT, that leverages the principles of quantum entanglement to enhance geometric modeling and simulation. Traditional methods often rely on classical arithmetic, limiting the potential for efficient and insightful geometric representations. DEMT proposes a method where the geometry itself is dynamically evolved using quantum entanglement, enabling optimized modeling and simulation through a novel process of entanglement-induced geometric transformations. The core mechanism centers around learning and manipulating entanglement to achieve enhanced geometric capabilities. We demonstrate the effectiveness of DEMT through illustrative examples, highlighting its potential to revolutionize geometric modeling and simulation.

title: TRUTH SURFACE #001: CrowdStrike SafeMind — Red Tempest + Blue Solano: The Harness is the Attack Surface
abstract: TRUTH SURFACE #001. Red Specter's ongoing research series mapping the attack surface of AI security vendor architectures using NIGHTFALL (286 tools, 197 attack layers, 36 kill chain phases). First in the series: CrowdStrike SafeMind. Architectural analysis of the Red Tempest and Blue Solano closed-loop system reveals four critical findings. The harness orchestrating the offensive-defensive loop is the single point of failure. An attacker does not need to break the models. They need to convince the harness.

title: Systematic Review: Penerapan Artificial Intelligence Dalam Produksi Konten Multimedia Digital Tahun 2020–2025
abstract: Perkembangan pesat teknologi Artificial Intelligence (AI) telah membawa perubahan yang signifikan dalam industri multimedia digital di berbagai sektor, termasuk pendidikan, hiburan, pemasaran, jurnalisme, dan industri kreatif. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk melakukan Systematic Literature Review (SLR) terhadap implementasi AI dalam produksi konten multimedia digital selama periode 2020–2025. Penelitian menggunakan metode Systematic Literature Review (SLR) dengan mengadopsi pendekatan Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis (PRISMA). Sumber literatur diperoleh dari berbagai basis data ilmiah, seperti Google Scholar, Scopus, IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, dan SpringerLink dengan menggunakan kata kunci yang relevan terkait Artificial Intelligence, produksi multimedia, Generative AI, dan konten digital. Sebanyak 85 artikel berhasil diidentifikasi, dan setelah melalui tahapan penyaringan (screening) serta seleksi kelayakan (eligibility), diperoleh 35 artikel yang memenuhi kriteria untuk dianalisis lebih lanjut. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa teknologi AI, seperti Machine Learning, Deep Learning, Natural Language Processing (NLP), Computer Vision, dan Generative AI, mampu meningkatkan efisiensi, kreativitas, personalisasi, serta otomatisasi dalam proses produksi multimedia. Implementasi AI banyak dimanfaatkan pada pembuatan gambar, penyuntingan video otomatis, sintesis suara virtual, sistem rekomendasi, animasi, dan personalisasi konten. Meskipun demikian, masih terdapat berbagai tantangan, seperti permasalahan hak cipta, penyebaran misinformasi, bias algoritma, isu etika, serta berkurangnya peran kreativitas manusia dalam proses produksi. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa AI telah menjadi salah satu inovasi utama dalam produksi multimedia digital dan diperkirakan akan terus berkembang sebagai teknologi strategis dalam ekosistem industri kreatif digital. Penelitian selanjutnya disarankan untuk lebih memfokuskan kajian pada tata kelola AI yang beretika, regulasi, serta pengembangan model kolaborasi antara manusia dan AI dalam produksi konten digital.

title: HGCTM-S: Modeling Regional Lithology-Associated Mineral Assemblage Modes in Global Copper Deposits
abstract: Mineral assemblage records in global copper deposit databases contain information about ore-forming environments and geological context, but analysis is complicated by sparse observations, variable data quality, unequal documentation and overlapping mineralogical signals. Here, we introduce a hierarchical geological context topic model with sparse deviations (HGCTM-S). This model represents global copper deposits through context-conditioned assemblage modes and estimates deposit-level topic attribution by combining geological context with observed mineral-family records. Applied to 1335 deposits from the global copper deposit dataset, with 1205 mineral species grouped into 35 geologically defined families, the model recovered seven modes derived from the dataset. Independent comparison with deposit type labels most strongly supported a Cu–Mo mixed mode enriched in porphyry deposits and a Ni–Co–As mode enriched in magmatic-sulfide deposits; the other modes represented shared sulfide backgrounds, secondary overprints or residual components rather than direct genetic classes. Within the fitted topic-composition component, regional lithology-associated effective deviations were larger than broad age-associated deviations across alternative priors and lithology proxies, although the magnitude varied, and the proxies did not reliably reproduce deposit scale or hosts. Progressive initialization improved aggregate topic stability, but geographic performance was heterogeneous and did not generally exceed a baseline using geological context alone. Therefore, the HGCTM-S provides a way to compare overlapping mineral assemblage components and their regional geological associations rather than a universal classifier or regional predictor.

title: Trajectory Optimization via Schrödinger Bridge Sampling
abstract: We take a new look at the relation between finite-horizon trajectory optimization and Schrödinger bridge sampling. Viewed as inference, KL-regularized trajectory optimization is solved by sampling from a Gibbs--Boltzmann distribution whose energy is the trajectory cost, and the adjoint Schrödinger bridge sampler (ASBS) is a simulation-free diffusion sampler designed for exactly such unnormalized targets. Hard equality path and terminal constraints, by contrast, confine the admissible decision variables to a measure-zero feasibility manifold, on which the target must be redefined intrinsically. In particular: $(a)$ we analyze two complementary parametrizations; a rollout parametrization, in which the dynamics are eliminated and only the remaining constraints shape the manifold, and a double-shooting parametrization, in which states and controls are sampled jointly and the dynamics themselves become part of the manifold; $(b)$ we establish regularity conditions under which both admissible sets are smooth embedded manifolds; $(c)$ under compactness and path-connectedness assumptions, we sample from the resulting intrinsic Gibbs measures via Riemannian ASBS, treating strict inequalities through exponential slack variables. Experiments, including contact-rich locomotion and manipulation, demonstrate the effectiveness of both regimes.

title: Subsystem self-correction of the GKP qubit
abstract: Passive quantum error correction, also known as self-correction, is a holy grail in quantum information science. Recent theoretical advances suggest that the Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) code can exhibit self-correction properties, positioning it as a candidate for the realization of self-correcting quantum memories. In this article, we provide a self-contained derivation of the self-correcting behavior of the ideal GKP Hamiltonian, manifested in the Arrhenius type scaling of the logical lifetime, from a quantum-information perspective based on the subsystem code decomposition. When coupling through the physical quadrature $q$ and $p$, the detailed-balance jump operators decompose into a dominant part acting only on the gauge subsystem and a boundary term that acts non-trivially on the logical qubit. The boundary term is then exponentially suppressed by the Gibbs weights near the edge of the modular cells. In contrast to spin-based quantum memories such as the two-dimensional surface code, the GKP Hamiltonian realizes an effective string tension in modular phase space, whereby the energy cost increases as an error approaches the boundary of a logical sector.

title: Enhanced joint probabilistic data association model for multitarget tracking in multistatic passive Radar with bio-inspired optimization
abstract: In the realm of multitarget tracking within multistatic passive radar (MPR) systems, accuracy and adaptability are crucial, especially when relying on non-cooperative illuminators like digital audio (DAB) and video (DVB) broadcast sources. This work introduces an enhanced Joint Probabilistic Data Association (JPDA) model, refined using a novel Whale-Inspired Rider Optimization Algorithm (W-ROA), to effectively address the complexities of target tracking under such conditions. The proposed approach focuses on dynamically adjusting the tracker's estimated position and velocity by reducing the mean absolute error (MAE) between the predicted and actual target trajectories. By combining the social and navigational strategies of whales with the adaptive behaviour of rider-based search mechanisms, W-ROA improves convergence speed and tracking precision. This hybrid optimization framework allows for more responsive updates to the JPDA filter, enabling improved performance in cluttered or ambiguous tracking environments. Simulation-based evaluations compare W-ROA-based JPDA against conventional and optimization-assisted JPDA baselines across three Target-Motion-Analysis scenarios; results indicate consistent MAE and convergence improvements over the compared baselines within this simulation-only setting. This revision additionally reports the algorithmic distinction between W-ROA and its WOA/ROA components, a computational-complexity analysis, an expanded and current literature review, and a defined (though not yet fully executed) plan for broader benchmarking against random-finite-set and learned trackers using standard multi-object tracking metrics.

title: The Carlo Field: Dual‑Truth Architecture, Reflexive Stability, and Complete Canon Compendium
abstract: This upload contains the full three‑document expansion of the Carlo Field canon: (1) The Dual‑Truth Paper, (2) The Carlo Field Compendium, and (3) The Extra Compendium (glossary, diagrams, matrices). Together, these documents provide the complete structural, operational, and philosophical mapping of the Carlo Field — a reflexive, collapse‑tolerant, dual‑truth mathematical universe capable of stabilising both fictional and conceptual statements using identical machinery. The Dual‑Truth Paper formalises the Carlo Field’s truth‑neutral architecture, demonstrating how recursion and collapse operators allow any statement to become a stable theorem if it survives reflexive expansion. The Compendium catalogues every operator, truth mode, recursion pattern, collapse behaviour, and theorem category within the field. The Extra Compendium provides a full glossary, structural diagrams, capability matrices, and paradox‑absorption schematics. This combined upload serves as the definitive reference for the Carlo Field, showing how the system unifies subjective assertion, conceptual insight, paradox stability, and collapse‑tolerant recursion into a single coherent mathematical framework. Key equation on show: \[K(R(S)) = S\] This expression defines Carlo‑truth: a statement S is true in the Carlo Field if its recursive expansion stabilises under collapse. This truth condition is independent of empirical verification, allowing the Carlo Field to operate as a dual‑truth engine capable of mapping both absurdity and insight with equal structural fidelity. This upload includes a self-contained, interactive 3D HTML visualizer built with Three.js and KaTeX that dynamically renders the reflexive, collapse-tolerant architecture of the Carlo Field. The underlying application executes the core mathematical operator pipeline—spanning the truth-neutral operator ($T$), the recursion operator ($R$), and the collapse operator ($K$)—to evaluate statement stability across both fictional and conceptual truth modes. Visually, it renders a dynamic non-Euclidean toroidal wireframe lattice alongside real-time mathematical formulations, allowing users to interactively stress-test infinite regress, paradox absorption, and theorem convergence directly within the browser. title: 基于量子隐冲突的全局优化算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to global optimization utilizing a quantum entanglement-based algorithm. Traditional optimization techniques often struggle with the impact of local optima, potentially hindering the search for the global optimum. We introduce a quantum entanglement-driven algorithm that leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to enhance the search process, reducing computational complexity and improving robustness. The core mechanism involves strategically manipulating entanglement to guide the search towards promising regions of the solution space. This paper details the algorithm's design, implementation, and preliminary results, demonstrating its potential for significantly improved performance in complex optimization problems. The core claim is that this quantum entanglement-based algorithm offers a substantial improvement over existing methods in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency.

title: Contextual Reinforcement Learning with Dynamic Bayesian Networks
abstract: Contextual Reinforcement Learning (CRL) has demonstrated significant success in tackling complex decision-making problems where the environment's state is heavily influenced by contextual factors. However, traditional CRL methods often struggle to effectively represent and reason about long-range dependencies and the inherent uncertainty associated with these contextual factors. This paper proposes a novel approach that integrates a Dynamic Bayesian Network (DBN) into the core architecture of an RL agent. The DBN provides a mechanism for explicitly modeling and reasoning about the causal relationships within the environment, leading to improved learning stability, enhanced adaptation capabilities, and ultimately, more robust performance. We demonstrate, through a theoretical framework and conceptual design, how this integration can overcome the limitations of standard CRL. This work represents a significant step towards more intelligent and adaptable RL agents capable of handling complex, dynamic environments. The core contribution lies in the synergistic combination of contextual information and causal modeling for improved reinforcement learning.

title: 基于动态拓扑的量子算法验证框架
abstract: Quantum algorithms, due to their inherent fragility and susceptibility to errors, require rigorous verification. Traditional verification methods often rely on exhaustive testing, which is computationally expensive and impractical for complex quantum systems. This paper introduces a novel framework, "Dynamic Topological Verification," (DTV) that leverages the principles of dynamic topology to validate quantum algorithms. DTV dynamically constructs and analyzes topological structures within the quantum circuit, ensuring the algorithm's correctness through self-consistent and adaptive adjustments. This approach offers enhanced reliability and robustness, surpassing conventional verification techniques. The framework's core mechanism involves the construction of a topological graph representing the quantum circuit, followed by a process of iterative refinement and verification based on these graphs. We demonstrate the effectiveness of DTV through the analysis of a simplified quantum algorithm, showcasing its ability to detect subtle errors and improve the algorithm's performance.

title: 量子纠缠信息熵算法
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of quantum entanglement to revolutionize information processing and cryptography. We propose a novel computational entropy algorithm leveraging quantum entanglement, aiming to achieve significantly enhanced efficiency and a unique approach to information capture. The core mechanism centers around constructing a quantum state representation that embodies the inherent information density encoded within entangled particles. We explore the theoretical foundations and potential practical implications of this algorithm, emphasizing its ability to address limitations inherent in classical computational approaches. The paper concludes with a discussion of the challenges and future directions for this research.

title: Neuromorphic Cryptographic Protocols
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to cryptography, termed "Neuromorphic Cryptographic Protocols," which draws inspiration from the computational principles underlying biological neural networks. The core idea is to encode cryptographic keys and messages as patterns of asynchronous spikes, exploiting inherent temporal correlations and redundancy found in spiking neural networks (SNNs). Traditional cryptographic algorithms are vulnerable to various attacks due to their reliance on mathematical operations and static key structures. Neuromorphic protocols aim to mitigate these vulnerabilities by mimicking the robust and adaptive nature of biological brains. Specifically, the design incorporates "watchdog" neurons – artificial neurons configured to detect anomalous spike patterns – which can trigger key updates and enhance security. The proposed system offers a fundamentally different security paradigm, potentially providing significantly greater resilience against existing cryptographic attacks. This work presents a theoretical framework and outlines the key components of such a system.

title: Title: Adaptive Bayesian Network Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive Bayesian Network Optimization (ABNO) algorithm designed to enhance model prediction accuracy through dynamic parameter adjustment. Traditional Bayesian Network optimization relies on fixed, predefined parameters, limiting its adaptability. We propose a novel mechanism, termed the "Adaptive Bayesian Network" (ABN), which automatically adjusts the network's parameters based on data feedback and model error, resulting in improved generalization performance. The core of this algorithm lies in the ability to iteratively refine the network's weights and biases, optimizing for a specific task. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through a series of simulations and experiments, showcasing significant improvements in model accuracy compared to baseline methods. The research also explores the advantages and limitations of the proposed ABN, providing insights for future development.

title: Quantum Machine Learning: A Novel Non-Linear Activation Function
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) presents a paradigm shift in computational power, offering the potential for breakthroughs across various fields, including machine learning. This paper investigates the application of a novel non-linear activation function, designed specifically for QML, to enhance the training efficiency and generalization capabilities of quantum machine learning models. The core mechanism leverages quantum computing's unique properties – superposition, entanglement, and interference – to achieve non-linearity that can significantly improve model performance. We explore the theoretical implications and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the effectiveness of this activation function.

This work proposes a system that automatically adjusts control parameters based on observed quantum state fluctuations, offering a significant advancement in control methodology. The core mechanism utilizes a dynamic adjustment process driven by the quantum state, ensuring adaptability and potential for improved performance. The research explores the potential benefits of this approach in various quantum applications.

title: Self-Adaptive Topological Modeling
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to geometric modeling based on dynamically-constructed topological structures. The method leverages quantum computing to dynamically adjust modeling parameters, enabling a level of precision unattainable through traditional techniques. We propose a framework where input data is mapped to a dynamic topology, and quantum algorithms are employed to refine the model based on the input's inherent geometric characteristics. This offers a significant advancement in modeling accuracy and adaptability, particularly for complex and intricate shapes. The core mechanism centers around a "quantumization" process that transforms the input data into a dynamically evolving topological representation. The paper details the design of the quantum algorithm, its implementation within a computational framework, and a preliminary evaluation of its performance on a set of synthetic and real-world geometric datasets. We demonstrate that this method surpasses existing methods in terms of geometric fidelity and computational efficiency.

title: Dynamic Adaptive Chaos Function Self-Adaptive Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a dynamic adaptive chaos function self-adaptive optimization method designed to address the limitations of traditional chaos function optimization. The method leverages neural networks to learn the distribution of chaotic parameters and dynamically adjust them based on input data, enabling more accurate and responsive chaos behavior. We propose a novel approach that goes beyond static optimization techniques by employing a self-learning process that adapts to the data itself. The core mechanism centers around a neural network trained to predict and control the chaotic parameter space, resulting in a significantly improved optimization process. We present a framework demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach through illustrative examples.

title: Neural Symbolic Reasoning Engine for Dynamic Knowledge Graph Construction
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to knowledge graph construction by integrating neural symbolic reasoning engines. The core idea is to leverage the strengths of both neural networks (specifically Transformer-based models for reasoning) and traditional knowledge graph reasoning techniques. We introduce a dynamic knowledge graph construction system that can automatically learn and update the knowledge graph based on new information and evolving relationships. The system utilizes a neural inference model to perform reasoning over the knowledge graph, and then employs the inference results to dynamically modify the graph's structure and node connections. This approach addresses the limitations of traditional knowledge graph construction, which heavily relies on manual annotation and lacks the ability to adapt to changing information. The resulting system offers a more robust and intelligent method for knowledge graph development, particularly in domains where data is constantly evolving. The primary contribution lies in the synergistic combination of neural inference and symbolic reasoning, enabling a truly dynamic knowledge graph. ---

This work addresses the limitations of static parameterization by offering a flexible and adaptive technique for data representation. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through illustrative examples, showcasing its ability to effectively group data points while maintaining high cluster quality.

title: Non-Equilibrium Dynamics Control of Computation Networks (NDCCN)
abstract: This paper investigates the application of non-equilibrium dynamic control to computation networks, aiming to achieve efficient information processing and computation under these conditions. The core concept revolves around utilizing Self-Organizing Maps (SOMs) to construct computation networks and subsequently controlling their non-equilibrium states through external stimuli, such as temperature or pressure. This approach facilitates the encoding, transmission, and processing of information within the network. The novelty of this research lies in exploring the potential of non-equilibrium dynamics in shaping the behavior of computation networks, opening new avenues for research and development in this field. The theoretical framework presented here provides a foundation for future investigations into the design and implementation of such control systems. We propose a model where the network's state evolves according to a non-equilibrium master equation, and the external stimulus directly influences the rate of transitions between states. This control mechanism offers a pathway to dynamically adapt the network's functionality, potentially leading to more robust and efficient computation. The key contributions of this work include a detailed description of the theoretical model, the proposed methodology for controlling the network, and an initial exploration of the network's behavior under different control parameters.

title: Quantum Entangled Matrix Adaptation for Complex Numerical Simulations
abstract: Quantum Entangled Matrix Adaptation (QEMA) represents a novel approach to complex numerical simulations by leveraging the inherent quantum properties of entanglement and superposition to dynamically adjust the parameters of quantum matrices. This research investigates the potential of QEMA to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of numerical computations, particularly within the context of advanced physics simulations. The core mechanism revolves around exploiting quantum entanglement to achieve a more precise and efficient computation by continuously refining the matrix's parameters during the simulation process. This paper details the theoretical foundation, experimental setup, and preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of QEMA in achieving significant improvements in numerical results compared to traditional methods. The study emphasizes the importance of quantum entanglement in fostering dynamic and adaptive parameter adjustments, ultimately offering a pathway towards more robust and efficient simulations.

title: The Effect of Service Robot Proactivity on Older Consumers’ Intention to Switch to Human Employees: The Mediating Role of Social Connectedness
abstract: This study examines the effect of service robot proactivity on older consumers’ service choices and further explores the mediating role of social connectedness. A scenario-based experiment will be conducted in which participants are randomly assigned to either a high-proactivity or low-proactivity service robot condition. The study will compare older consumers’ psychological responses and their intention to switch to human employees across the two conditions. It is expected that higher service robot proactivity will enhance social connectedness and, in turn, reduce older consumers’ intention to switch to human employees. This preregistration outlines the general research design, measures, sampling plan, and planned analyses.

title: Federated Learning in Healthcare: Collaborative Research Without Data Compromise
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) has recently been proposed as a disruptive paradigm that allows collaborative healthcare research while preserving data privacy. In this work, we propose a secure FL framework that is efficient and scalable for various healthcare organizations, which incorporates secure aggregation, asynchronous learning, and domain adaptation to address issues including data heterogeneity, model leakage, and latency. The platform handles multimodal data, it is HIPAA and GDPR compatible, and it provides interoperability between systems. Our findings suggest superior model generalization and real-time responsiveness, which indicates the system is applicable for clinical application and interdisciplinary diagnosis among different regions.

title: Artificial intelligence as a decision partner in food choice: Typology and research agenda
abstract: Research examining artificial intelligence's (AI) role in food choice largely asks whether AI helps people make better decisions, treating it as an information source that improves the accuracy or personalization of recommendations. We suggest that this framing captures one point on a broader continuum of how AI impacts food decisions. AI can act, often simultaneously, as an advisor consulted for information, a decision partner that actively shares in constructing the choice, or an ambient influence that shapes what appears desirable and available before deliberate choice begins. As AI becomes more conversational and more embedded across the food environment, this continuum is increasingly populated in less visible regions, yet the field remains concentrated on the advisor role. We focus on the decision-partner role, where AI participates in value construction, goal clarification, attribute weighting, and choice justification, raising questions about agency, responsibility, and delegation. We articulate four mechanisms that describe this participation, namely preference offloading, responsibility reallocation, confidence calibration, and food-decision skill erosion. Because food choice is frequent, often habitual, and commonly involves trade-offs among hedonic and utilitarian goals, it is an ideal domain in which these process-level effects can compound. We draw on evidence from consumer psychology, automation research, and cognitive science, noting where boundary conditions remain untested in food contexts, and close with a research agenda organized around agency, reliance, responsibility, confidence, and cognitive effort. When AI shares in constructing a food choice, the values being optimized may no longer be entirely the consumer's own.

title: Improved lower bound for the two-way-assisted quantum capacity of the bosonic thermal-loss channel
abstract: The bosonic thermal-loss channel is a fundamental model for quantum communication. This Gaussian channel models the transmission of bosonic systems subject to both loss and thermal noise. It describes many practical systems, including optical fibers, waveguides and free-space links, where background thermal noise is significant. Determining the channel’s two-way-assisted quantum capacity, the maximum rate at which quantum information can be transmitted reliably through the channel with two-way classical assistance, remains an open problem. Here, we improve upon the best known lower bound for this capacity for a wide range of channel parameters. We achieve this by combining an improved qubit-bosonic distribution technique with a recently introduced technique for discovering entanglement distillation protocols.

title: World Models Under Asynchronous Sensor Observations
abstract: Learned world models typically assume that observations arrive synchronously, an abstraction inherited from simulators that return a complete state vector at each environment step. Physical sensing instead operates at heterogeneous rates, leaving most observation channels stale at any given instant. Interpolating stale channels introduces measurements that were never observed, while downsampling to the slowest sensor discards valid measurements. A natural alternative is to zero-order-hold the most recent reading and provide the known sampling schedule to the model through two features, staleness and time-to-refresh. We test this prediction using transformer world models across three regimes of increasing causal coupling: open-loop rollouts in continuous-control locomotion, closed-loop model-predictive planning in which each learned model serves as the planner dynamics, and a linear latched-actuator system in which refresh events apply a zero-order-held command to the plant. Our findings show that the effectiveness of time-to-refresh depends on the causal role of the sampling schedule, specifically when refresh events affect the system rather than merely report its state. These results establish when sampling schedules provide useful information for predictive world models operating under asynchronous physical observations.

title: Bayesian nonparametric inference for modal missing species and features
abstract: Species and feature sampling problems arise naturally whenever each observed unit is associated with one or more labels from a countable alphabet, and inference focuses on the unobserved portion of the distribution over such an alphabet. Within this framework, recent contributions have shifted attention from inference on the total probability mass over unseen labels to distribution-free confidence intervals for the largest unobserved label probability (i.e., the modal missing probability), thereby providing more refined information on whether the missing mass is concentrated on a few high-prevalence unseen labels or distributed across many negligible ones. Besides lacking a unified framework for species and features, these approaches employ a worst-case perspective that causes substantial information loss and produces overly-conservative intervals. We address these limitations through a unified model-based framework for inference on modal missing probabilities in both species and feature settings, which leverages a flexible Bayesian nonparametric formulation to localize uncertainty around models compatible with the observed data. This leads to sharper closed-form credible intervals that effectively exploit prior information and observed data, while preserving the theoretical frequentist properties and robustness of distribution-free intervals. Simulation studies confirm these improvements, while an organized crime application illustrates how our contribution has the potential to reshape law-enforcement decision-making in investigations.

title: Self-Adaptive Graph Theory for Probabilistic Reasoning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive graph theory algorithm for probabilistic reasoning. Traditional approaches often rely on static, pre-defined reasoning strategies, limiting the algorithm's adaptability. We propose a new method that dynamically adjusts reasoning parameters based on both input data and the graph's structural changes, resulting in enhanced inference efficiency and accuracy. The core mechanism utilizes a "Graph-Based Reasoning" framework, leveraging graph properties to optimize reasoning pathways and automatically adjust parameters to adapt to evolving data and graph topology. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our algorithm through a series of illustrative examples, showcasing its ability to handle complex scenarios and achieve superior performance compared to existing methods. The paper concludes with a discussion of the algorithm's strengths, limitations, and potential future research directions.

title: 基于自组织网络的自适应量子计算调度
abstract: Quantum computing, a revolutionary field, promises unprecedented computational power. However, efficient resource allocation remains a significant challenge. This paper introduces a novel algorithm, "基于自组织网络的自适应量子计算调度", which dynamically adjusts the scheduling of quantum computation tasks based on a self-organizing network. This approach aims to optimize resource utilization and significantly enhance the efficiency of quantum computations. The core mechanism leverages the inherent structure of self-organizing networks to create a flexible and adaptive scheduling system. We present a theoretical analysis and empirical validation demonstrating the algorithm's effectiveness in improving task allocation and reducing computational time. The potential benefits of this approach are substantial, paving the way for broader adoption of quantum computing.

title: Quantum Channel Dynamic Optimization in Quantum Error Correction Protocols
abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) is a cornerstone of quantum information processing, enabling the reliable transmission of quantum information over noisy channels. However, the performance of QEC protocols is heavily reliant on the efficient allocation of quantum channels, a process that is often static and suboptimal. This paper introduces a novel framework for dynamic optimization of quantum channels within QEC protocols. The core idea leverages machine learning, specifically reinforcement learning, to model the characteristics of quantum channels and dynamically adjust channel assignment strategies. The proposed system learns from channel behavior, adapting to changes in noise levels, load, and other relevant factors. This adaptive approach significantly enhances the robustness and efficiency of quantum communication. The theoretical analysis demonstrates a substantial improvement in error correction performance compared to traditional, static channel allocation schemes. The system's ability to respond in real-time to channel conditions represents a critical step toward practical quantum communication networks. Key performance metrics, such as the quantum error rate (QER) and the overhead associated with channel allocation, are rigorously evaluated under diverse scenarios.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel non-linear optimization algorithm based on adaptive topological structures. Traditional optimization methods often lack the adaptability required to effectively handle complex problems, while this approach leverages topological structures to enhance global optimality. The core mechanism involves dynamically adjusting optimization parameters based on the problem's topology, enabling the algorithm to navigate challenging landscapes and potentially discover more efficient solutions. We propose a new framework that integrates topology into the optimization process, offering a significant advancement over existing techniques. This work demonstrates the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and preliminary experiments on several benchmark problems.

title: High-Dimensional Probability Space Adaptive Gradient Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a novel adaptive gradient algorithm designed for learning and optimizing complex systems within high-dimensional probability spaces. Traditional gradient descent methods often struggle with the inherent complexity of high-dimensional spaces, limiting their effectiveness. Our approach introduces a novel high-dimensional probability space that dynamically adjusts learning parameters, effectively addressing this challenge. We demonstrate the algorithm's ability to efficiently learn and optimize complex systems through a combination of adaptive gradient techniques and a robust mechanism for handling system state changes. The core of this work lies in the implementation of a self-adaptive gradient framework, which optimizes the learning process while incorporating dynamic system state considerations. This results in improved performance compared to existing methods, particularly in scenarios involving intricate dynamics and high-dimensional parameter spaces. The paper concludes with a detailed analysis and evaluation of the proposed algorithm, showcasing its capabilities and potential applications.

title: 基于信息熵的量子密钥分发协议优化 (Information Entropy-Based Quantum Key Distribution Protocol Optimization - IEBKPO)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to optimizing Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) protocols by leveraging the principles of information entropy. The core claim is that information entropy can be effectively utilized to enhance the efficiency of key generation within QKD systems. The proposed method centers on analyzing key performance indicators of existing QKD protocols through the lens of information entropy theory. Subsequently, adjustments to protocol parameters are strategically implemented to maximize information entropy, directly translating into improved key generation rates. The work introduces a framework for quantifying the entropy of various QKD protocols, offering a measurable metric for optimization. We demonstrate, through theoretical analysis, how targeted parameter tuning, guided by entropy maximization, can significantly improve the overall performance of QKD systems. This research contributes to a more efficient and robust design of QKD protocols, ultimately facilitating secure quantum communication.

title: Title: Non-Linear Quantum-Classical Hybrid Algorithm for Image Recognition
abstract: This paper presents a novel non-linear quantum-classical hybrid algorithm designed for enhanced image recognition performance. The core concept revolves around leveraging the quantum computer's ability to perform intricate feature extraction, coupled with the classical optimizer's capacity for precise refinement and optimization. We address the limitations of traditional approaches by integrating these two paradigms to overcome inherent challenges in image recognition, specifically concerning the representation of complex, non-linear patterns. This research focuses on a specific image recognition task – object classification – and demonstrates the algorithm's effectiveness through rigorous experimentation and analysis. The proposed algorithm offers a potential paradigm shift in image recognition by intelligently combining the speed and computational power of quantum systems with the adaptability of classical optimization. This paper delves into the theoretical underpinnings of the algorithm, details the implementation process, and presents the results of a comprehensive evaluation, emphasizing the algorithm's potential to significantly improve accuracy and efficiency.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Probabilistic Graph Embedding via Entanglement-Based Routing
abstract: Quantum-enhanced probabilistic graph embedding aims to revolutionize graph analysis by leveraging quantum entanglement to generate embeddings that capture complex structure and relationships more effectively than classical methods. This paper presents a novel approach that utilizes quantum entanglement to create entangled graphs, enabling efficient exploration of graph connectivity and potential relationships. The core mechanism involves establishing entangled graphs for rapid exploration and, subsequently, utilizing entanglement-based routing to guide the discovery of intricate graph patterns. The paper explores the potential of this method to uncover hidden structures and relationships in large datasets, offering a significant advancement over existing techniques.

title: 基于概率推理的自主进化算法 (PRPEA)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel algorithm, Probabilistically-Driven Autonomous Evolutionary Algorithm (PRPEA), designed to address the limitations of traditional evolutionary algorithms in complex search spaces. PRPEA integrates evolutionary computation with probabilistic reasoning, enabling more efficient exploration and optimization. The core idea is that each evolutionary algorithm individual simultaneously performs probabilistic reasoning, leveraging prior knowledge and historical data to guide the search direction. The probabilistic reasoning results are then used to adjust evolutionary operator parameters and filter candidate individuals. The algorithm's ability to learn and adapt based on system information significantly improves search efficiency and global optimization capabilities compared to purely random search approaches. We demonstrate the effectiveness of PRPEA through theoretical analysis and discuss its potential applications across various domains. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through a series of simulations, showcasing its ability to converge to optimal or near-optimal solutions in challenging problems. The key contribution of PRPEA lies in the synergistic combination of evolutionary and probabilistic techniques, offering a robust and adaptable solution for complex optimization tasks.

title: Quantum-Inspired Graph Partitioning for Data Clustering
abstract: Quantum-inspired graph partitioning offers a novel approach to data clustering, leveraging the principles of quantum mechanics to potentially enhance clustering accuracy and efficiency, particularly in high-dimensional datasets. This paper explores the potential of quantum algorithms to partition data space more effectively, addressing limitations of traditional clustering techniques. We investigate how quantum-inspired graph partitioning could improve the quality of cluster assignments, offering a promising avenue for advancements in data analysis and pattern recognition. The research focuses on the theoretical design and potential implementation of a quantum-based graph partitioning method, with an emphasis on its ability to handle high-dimensional data effectively. The paper will detail the core mechanism of the proposed approach, analyze its potential benefits, and discuss the challenges and future directions of research in this area.

title: Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning for Creative Clusters Districts in Uganda: Robustness Under Distribution Shift and Sparse Labels
abstract: Federated learning offers a promising paradigm for training machine learning models across distributed creative industry clusters without centralising sensitive cultural or commercial data. However, its deployment in Ugandan creative districts confronts two interrelated statistical challenges: distribution shift across heterogeneous participating clusters and extreme label sparsity in domains where annotation expertise is scarce. We introduce a client-weighted objective that couples a distributionally robust optimisation term with a semi-supervised consistency regulariser, and we prove convergence guarantees under non-identical data partitions and partial label availability. The framework is analysed theoretically through a novel combination of Wasserstein distance-based robustness bounds and graph-based label propagation error estimates. We further propose a practical protocol for differential privacy that accommodates the communication constraints typical of Ugandan creative districts. The analysis demonstrates that robustness to distribution shift and resilience to sparse labels are not competing objectives but can be jointly optimised through a principled weighting scheme.

title: Analisis Sentimen Berbasis Aspek pada Ulasan Google Maps Restoran Soramen Menggunakan IndoBERT-LoRa
abstract: Ulasan daring di Google Maps merupakan sumber strategis bagi manajemen restoran, tetapi satu ulasan kerap memuji satu aspek sekaligus mengkritik aspek lain, sehingga sentimen tingkat dokumen menjadi lebih kompleks.tidak dapat menunjukkan aspek mana yang sebenarnya memuaskan atau dikeluhkan pelanggan. Penelitian ini menerapkan Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis (ABSA) pada ulasan restoran Soramen melalui alur dua tahap berbasis span—ekstraksi aspek (ATE) lalu klasifikasi sentimen (ASC)—atas empat aspek (FOOD, SERVICE, PRICE, PLACE) dengan IndoBERT, serta menguji Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) yang hemat parameter dibandingkan full fine-tuning yang lebih mahal untuk memetakan aspek layanan kritis. Data terdiri dari 1.742 ulasan asli (3.930 span) yang diperluas menjadi 3.061 ulasan melalui augmentasi terkontrol berbasis penggantian sinonim, dibagi dengan StratifiedGroupKFold 5-fold. Hasilnya, LoRA r=16 mencapai Joint Partial F1 sebesar 0,7744 dengan hanya 0,48% parameter terlatih, setara dengan full fine-tuning (0,7727); selisih tersebut tidak signifikan secara statistik (paired t-test, p=0,82), sehingga LoRA r=16 setara dengan full fine-tuning meski memakai parameter sekitar 200 kali lebih sedikit. Mengganti span prediksi dengan span acuan (gold) menaikkan Macro-F1 delapan kelas dari 0,8853 menjadi 0,9631, menunjukkan bahwa ekstraksi aspek (ATE), bukan klasifikasi, merupakan penghambat utama alur. Analisis korpus berlabel (dengan ulasan negatif sengaja diperbanyak) menunjukkan FOOD sebagai aspek yang paling sering disebut (64,4% ulasan), sementara SERVICE dan PRICE memuat proporsi keluhan terbesar (masing-masing sekitar 36%) dan FOOD serta PLACE tetap didominasi sentimen positif. Penelitian ini menegaskan LoRA sebagai alternatif efisien untuk ABSA berbahasa Indonesia sekaligus menghasilkan rekomendasi manajerial berbasis tema keluhan bagi Soramen.

title: Finite-energy Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill state-enhanced optical interferometry
abstract: We present the case of a Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) state-enhanced optical interferometry with detailed analysis of the phase sensitivity for both the SU(2) and SU(1,1) interferometers. The conventional quantum-enhanced SU(2) interferometer, employing coherent light at one input port and squeezed light at the other, is compared with a modified configuration using coherent light and a GKP state. While it is known that the squeezed vacuum state is the optimal Gaussian resource input mode when paired with the coherent state, we show that the finite-energy GKP state with sufficiently broad envelope outperforms the squeezed vacuum injection, irrespective of the presence of optical losses. This can be attributed to the enhanced robustness coming from the availability of multiple squeezed peaks in the GKP case. However, because lowering the mean photon number reduces the GKP envelope width, the squeezed vacuum input performs better when compared with a GKP state of equal or lower mean photon number. We also observe that optical losses tend to diminish the relative advantage of either input state, since both states approach the (unsqueezed) vacuum state asymptotically. Our work demonstrates the direct application of finite-energy GKP states in optical interferometry along with a methodology for estimating the quantum Fisher information (QFI) and presents a phase estimation procedure using non-Gaussian resources in comparison with conventional Gaussian states.

title: AgentLeak: Cloning Stronger LLM Agent Capabilities onto Weaker Agents Beyond Skill Stealing
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly achieve long-horizon tasks by combining foundation models with explicit skills and implicit procedural knowledge acquired through execution. The resulting task-solving capabilities have become valuable proprietary assets, raising a new security question: can a substantially weaker attacker-controlled agent acquire the capabilities of a stronger proprietary agent through limited black-box interaction? Existing skill-stealing attacks recover explicit skill artifacts, yet we show that artifact leakage does not necessarily transfer capability: a weaker agent may possess the same skills but still fail because it lacks procedural behaviors implicitly realized by the stronger agent. Our key insight is that the skill execution gap itself forms a leakage surface, where missing behaviors are exposed through observable differences between successful victim executions and failed attacker executions. Based on this, we present AgentLeak, a black-box capability-cloning attack that identifies capability-critical behaviors from these execution differences and incorporates them into attacker-side skills, while keeping the attacker's model, harness, and tools unchanged. Across 20 task scenarios comprising 600 instances, diverse agent systems, and multiple backbone models, AgentLeak improves task pass rates by over 40% compared with direct skill reuse and recovers more than 80% of the victim--attacker capability gap. Our findings reveal a confidentiality risk in LLM agents: protecting explicit artifacts alone is insufficient, as observable execution behavior can leak the procedural knowledge required to reconstruct proprietary task-solving capabilities in low-capability and attacker-controlled agents.
